column2: Guild help
column3: Gildets hjelp

column2:
Honourable {%R:04} Jantzen! 

I have seen you questioning the people in the markets and the narrow streets of Oslo. This aroused my attention; then such behaviour is not befitting to a man of your rank.
As I have been told, you are looking for Jakob Blank. This poor beggar was taken for a ride by your "fine" society and came to us for protection in order to disappear unnoticed. Pardon! I forgot to introduce myself. My name is really not of any significance, suffice to say, that I chair the local guild. I am sure you understand what I mean, and whilst not wanting to appear too arrogant - I do not indeed, look like a vagabond. 
We took Jakob Blank away into a secure country area at the time, and the colleagues there did such a good job that not even I can say where he is at the moment. But I would certainly have heard of his death. 
Because you appear to be his friend, I will support you in your inquires. For me to do that, you will have to acquire a reputation of trust in the community otherwise I won't be able to do anything for you. When your name becomes known in the right circles, you will get the required information almost automatically.

Farewell,
\f5_X
column3:
Aerede {%R:04} Jantzen!

Jeg har sett Dem spoerre ut folk paa torgene og i smugene i Oslo. Det vakte min oppmerksomhet, for en slik oppfoersel soemmer seg ikke for en mann av Deres rang.
Som jeg har hoert, leter De etter Jakob Blank. Denne stakkars fyren ble lurt av Deres "fine" selskap og kom til oss for aa faa beskyttelse og forsvinne ubemerket. Unnskyld! Jeg glemte aa presentere meg. Mitt navn er virkelig uten betydning; la det vaere nok aa si at jeg er formann i det lokale gildet. De forstaar sikkert hva jeg mener, og uten aa ville virke for hovmodig - jeg ser jo ikke ut som en landstryker.
Vi foerte den gang Jakob Blank til en sikker egn, og kollegene der gjorde saa godt arbeid at ikke engang jeg kan si hvor han er naa. Men om hans doed ville jeg sikkert ha hoert.
Siden De synes aa vaere hans venn, skal jeg stoette Dem i Deres etterforskning. Til det maa De vinne fellesskapets tillit, ellers kan jeg ikke gjoere noe for Dem. Naar Deres navn blir kjent i de rette kretser, faar De de noedvendige opplysningene nesten av seg selv.

Farvel,
\f5_X

column2: Stetin
column3: Stettin

column2: The searched person is in Stetin.\n\n\\f5_X
column3: Den ettersoekte befinner seg i Stettin.\n\n\\f5_X

column2:
Dear Leopold Jantzen!

I have made so much effort to leave the misfortunes of the past behind me. However, when I heard about the death of your father, I knew that you would be looking for me and that my old debt had caught up with me again.
I am sure you have come to ask me about the  "flying trader". I will tell you what I know, but before that you'll have to do something for me.
Take me to grave of my old friend in Lubeck so that I can pray for his and my eternal soul!
I will wait on your ship {%s:09} for you.

Jakob Blank
column3:
Kjaere Leopold Jantzen!

Jeg har gjort saa mye for aa legge fortidens ulykker bak meg. Men da jeg hoerte om Deres fars doed, visste jeg at De ville lete etter meg, og at min gamle skyld igjen hadde innhentet meg.
De er sikkert kommet for aa spoerre meg om "Den flygende handelsmann". Jeg skal fortelle hva jeg vet, men foerst maa De gjoere noe for meg.
Foer meg til min gamle venns grav i Luebeck, saa jeg kan be for hans og min evige sjel!
Jeg venter paa Dem paa Deres skip {%s:09}.

Jakob Blank

column2: Inheritance
column3: Arv

column2:
Announcement of the decision concerning the estate of the Lubecker citizen and Patrician, Georg Jantzen.

On the basis of an old document that was stored in the archives of Bremen and Lubeck, the officials of the said towns, have jointly come to the following agreement:

As agreed in writing at the time, the Bremer Patrician Vanderdeeken inherits the estate of the Jantzens of Lubeck. Besides monies, the assets also include movables and immovable, such as ships and buildings.

Other assets to be transferred include the forenamed values of the  {%R:04} Leopold Jantzen, where it can be proved that a substantial part of it came from his father's estate. 
The transfer will take place in five days.

{%+:01}
column3:
Kunngjoering av beslutningen om doedsboet etter Luebeck-borgeren og patrisieren Georg Jantzen.

Paa grunnlag av et gammelt dokument som ble oppbevart i arkivene i Bremen og Luebeck, er embetsmennene i de nevnte byene i fellesskap kommet frem til foelgende ordning:

Som den gang avtalt skriftlig arver patrisieren Vanderdeeken fra Bremen familien Jantzens bo i Luebeck. I tillegg til penger omfatter formuen ogsaa loesoere og fast eiendom, som skip og bygninger.

Til formuen som skal overdras, hoerer dessuten de foernevnte verdiene til {%R:04} Leopold Jantzen, i den grad det kan paavises at en vesentlig del stammer fra hans fars bo.
Overdragelsen finner sted om fem dager.

{%+:01}

column2: Stranger
column3: Fremmed

column2:
Dear Sir!

A peculiar stranger was inquiring about you in the harbour area of {%t:08}. He was wearing a long black habit, and his appearance sent shivers down my spine.
However, because you are waiting for an urgent message, whose source is not so important, I have sent the stranger to you.

Greetings,Sailor {%V:0F} from {%s:09}
column3:
Herre!

En underlig fremmed har spurt etter Dem i havnen i {%t:08}. Han bar en lang svart kutte, og synet av ham fikk det til aa gaa kaldt nedover ryggen paa meg.
Men siden De venter paa et hastende budskap, der opphavet ikke er saa viktig, har jeg sendt den fremmede til Dem.

Hilsen, matros {%V:0F} paa {%s:09}

column2: Offer
column3: Tilbud

column2:
Leopold Jantzen!

It is wonderful to personally make your acquaintance. I knew your father, a very pleasant person - until he fell victim to madness. I hear you are looking for Jakob Blank. Yet another acquaintance of mine, unfortunately I do not even know myself, where he is at the moment.But I have been observing you for a while now. You are someone who could go quite far; I can feel something like that immediately. You only need a little support from the side of influence. I can offer you this support. You'll see, with me working for you in the background everything will develop to your advantage. Without me, however, some wishes are unattainable. I'll give you the choice:

Do you want to become rich and famous with me? Or do you want to risk being crushed between the millstones of intrigue if you pursue the rough road to the summit?
What I demand for my support is nothing more than a fair share of your future wealth. Decide wisely!
column3:
Leopold Jantzen!

Det er en glede aa gjoere Deres personlige bekjentskap. Jeg kjente Deres far, et svaert behagelig menneske - til han falt som offer for galskapen. Jeg hoerer at De leter etter Jakob Blank. Enda en av mine bekjente; dessverre vet jeg ikke selv hvor han er for oeyeblikket. Men jeg har iakttatt Dem en stund. De er en som kan naa langt; slikt kjenner jeg med en gang. De trenger bare litt stoette fra innflytelsesrikt hold. Den stoetten kan jeg tilby Dem. De skal se: med meg virkende for Dem i bakgrunnen vil alt utvikle seg til Deres fordel. Uten meg forblir derimot visse oensker uoppnaaelige. Jeg gir Dem valget:

Vil De bli rik og beroemt med meg? Eller vil De risikere aa bli knust mellom intrigenes kvernsteiner om De gaar den bratte veien mot toppen?
Det jeg krever for min stoette, er ikke annet enn en rimelig andel av Deres fremtidige rikdom. Velg klokt!

column2: Support
column3: Ta imot stoette

column2: Forget it!
column3: Glem det!

column2: Follow
column3: Foelg

column2:
Leopold Jantzen!

Your rejection of this generous offer offends me. You alone will bear the responsibility for this decision. I did warn you!

Farewell!
column3:
Leopold Jantzen!

Deres avvisning av dette rause tilbudet krenker meg. De alene baerer ansvaret for denne beslutningen. Jeg advarte Dem!

Farvel!

column2: Contract
column3: Kontrakt

column2:
Leopold Jantzen!

Your decision was clever and will make you into a rich and powerful man. You must in fact pay for a few of your father's mistakes but after that, nothing will hold you back.
You will hear from again when the time is right.

Until then.
column3:
Leopold Jantzen!

Deres beslutning var klok og vil gjoere Dem til en rik og mektig mann. Riktignok maa De betale for noen av Deres fars feiltrinn, men deretter vil ingenting holde Dem tilbake.
De vil hoere fra meg igjen naar tiden er inne.

Til da.

column2: Generous
column3: Raus

column2:
Poor Leopold!

You will certainly be surprised over the change in circumstances and disappointed over your own poverty. But, how should you have known what agreements the good old Georg was capable of entering into, just to further his career.
I said that we were old acquaintances, your father and I, and although he always looked down at me, I now feel almost sorry for you in your situation - To be cheated of what one has built up by ones own father. Whilst I'm in a good mood, I'll let you have something from the estate that now legally belongs to me. I do not need a second trading office in Lubeck, and I now really have a surplus of ships and small change.
You do not have to thank me for my generosity, just simply stay out of my way in future.

H. Vanderdeeken
{%-:00}HV
column3:
Stakkars Leopold!

De er sikkert overrasket over de endrede forholdene og skuffet over Deres egen fattigdom. Men hvordan skulle De ha visst hvilke avtaler gode gamle Georg var i stand til aa inngaa, bare for aa fremme sin loepebane?
Jeg sa jo at vi var gamle bekjente, Deres far og jeg, og selv om han alltid saa ned paa meg, synes jeg naa nesten synd paa Dem i Deres situasjon - aa bli fraroevet av sin egen far det man selv har bygd opp. Siden jeg er i godt humoer, lar jeg Dem faa noe av boet som naa rettmessig tilhoerer meg. Jeg trenger ikke noe annet kontor i Luebeck, og skip og smaapenger har jeg virkelig i overflod.
De trenger ikke takke meg for rausheten; hold Dem bare unna meg i fremtiden.

H. Vanderdeeken
{%-:00}HV

column2: Home journey
column3: Hjemreise

column2:
Dear young Jantzen!

I prayed at the grave of your father for both of our souls. I now feel strong enough to tell you about the "flying trader", however not here in Lubeck.
The curse, which hung over your father, is even effective beyond the grave and affects the whole family. My luck that I never married.
Take me back to Stetin! I will satisfy your inquisitiveness in my home.
I will again wait for you in the harbour tavern.

Jakob Blank
column3:
Kjaere unge Jantzen!

Jeg har bedt ved Deres fars grav for vaare begges sjeler. Naa foeler jeg meg sterk nok til aa fortelle om "Den flygende handelsmann", men ikke her i Luebeck.
Forbannelsen som hvilte over Deres far, virker til og med hinsides graven og rammer hele slekten. Heldig for meg at jeg aldri giftet meg.
Foer meg tilbake til Stettin! I mitt hjem skal jeg stille Deres nysgjerrighet.
Jeg venter igjen paa Dem paa havnevertshuset.

Jakob Blank

column2: Devil ship
column3: Djevelskip

column2:
Dear young Jantzen!

Thank you for the safe journey home! As promised, I will now tell you about the journey on which your father and I met the  "flying trader".
I'm sure you have already heard the story of the  "flying trader", haven't you? The "flying trader" is a ghost ship that wanders the North and Baltic Seas. Its captain was a greedy trader who went into consorts with the devil to increase his fortune. And he amassed a great fortune, which he jealously guarded on his huge ship.
One day however, the devil demanded the return of his share, but the mean trader refused to pay.
The devil laughed at him, he would get his own back.  He dammed the trader never to leave his ship full of gold, and in addition to that, never to find a place of rest until the end of time.  The  "flying trader" has been sailing the Northern Seas with his ghost ship ever since then and brings misfortunes to seamen who come across his ship.
That's enough for today, as you can see, my hands are shaking from recalling the story. Let me rest for a day and I will then tell you the rest of the story.

Jakob Blank
column3:
Kjaere unge Jantzen!

Takk for den trygge hjemreisen! Som lovet skal jeg naa fortelle om reisen der Deres far og jeg moette "Den flygende handelsmann".
De har sikkert allerede hoert historien om "Den flygende handelsmann", ikke sant? "Den flygende handelsmann" er et spoekelsesskip som flakker omkring paa Nordsjoeen og Oestersjoeen. Kapteinen var en graadig handelsmann som inngikk pakt med djevelen for aa oeke formuen sin. Og han samlet en stor formue, som han sjalu voktet paa sitt veldige skip.
Men en dag krevde djevelen sin andel tilbake, og den gjerrige handelsmannen nektet aa betale.
Djevelen lo av ham: han skulle nok faa sin hevn. Han forbannet handelsmannen til aldri aa forlate sitt skip fullt av gull og dessuten aldri aa finne hvile til tidenes ende. Siden den gang seiler "Den flygende handelsmann" paa de nordlige hav med spoekelsesskipet sitt og bringer ulykke over sjoefolk som moeter skipet hans.
Nok for i dag; som De ser, skjelver hendene mine bare av aa minnes historien. La meg hvile en dag, saa forteller jeg resten.

Jakob Blank

column2: Encounter
column3: Moete

column2:
Dear young Jantzen!

I promised to tell you the second part of the story today, and I'll keep my word.Your father was a young trader at the time, exactly as you are at the moment. He did not have a lot and captained his snaikka the "Morning Greetings", on which I served as helmsman.
We were on our way with a cargo from Bremen, when a sail appeared on the horizon and quickly came nearer. We quickly realised what was coming towards us, then the "Morning Greetings" had just sailed into a calm. It could only be a ghost ship, and it was flying across the waves at full sail. Everyone at that time knew the story of the "flying trader", and as the ghost ship's dinghy rowed towards us, we hid ourselves behind some barrels.
As a ghostlike shape stepped on board and loudly shouted for the captain of the ship, your father and I sprang into the dinghy and fled as quickly as we could row.We made inquires about "Morning Greetings" at the next port, but it was nowhere to be seen. There was still no news of it in the weeks that followed, so we reported it as sunk in the storm, and cashed in on the insurance. 
However, your father and I had let it down, although we were the most experienced sailors on board. We never got rid of this feeling of guilt. 
I can tell from the expression on your face - that you do not believe a single word -, and only believe that, which you can see with your own eyes.
I could give you a chart showing the exact position of the "flying trader", but I do not want have anymore dead sailors on my conscience.
You'll have to form an armed fleet: If you have a ship, which you can use as an Orlogship, then I will show you the location. If you then sailed to your grave in such a fleet, it wouldn't be my fault.

Jakob Blank
column3:
Kjaere unge Jantzen!

Jeg lovet aa fortelle historiens andre del i dag, og jeg holder ord. Deres far var den gang en ung handelsmann, akkurat som De er naa. Han eide ikke mye og foerte sin schnigge "Morgenhilsen", der jeg tjente som styrmann.
Vi var paa vei med en last fra Bremen da et seil dukket opp i horisonten og raskt kom naermere. Vi forsto snart hva som naermet seg, for "Morgenhilsen" hadde nettopp kommet i stille. Det kunne bare vaere et spoekelsesskip, og det floey over boelgene for fulle seil. Alle kjente den gang historien om "Den flygende handelsmann", og da spoekelsesskipets jolle rodde mot oss, gjemte vi oss bak noen toenner.
Da en spoekelsesaktig skikkelse steg om bord og hoeylytt ropte etter skipets kaptein, hoppet Deres far og jeg i jollen og flyktet saa fort vi kunne ro. I neste havn spurte vi etter "Morgenhilsen", men den var ikke aa se noe sted. Heller ikke i ukene etterpaa kom det nytt, saa vi meldte den forlist i stormen og hevet forsikringen.
Likevel hadde Deres far og jeg sviktet den, selv om vi var de mest erfarne sjoefolkene om bord. Den skyldfoelelsen ble vi aldri kvitt.
Jeg ser paa ansiktet Deres at De ikke tror et ord og bare tror det De ser med egne oeyne.
Jeg kunne gi Dem et sjoekart med den noeyaktige posisjonen til "Den flygende handelsmann", men jeg vil ikke ha flere doede sjoefolk paa samvittigheten.
De maa danne en vaepnet flaate: har De et skip De kan bruke som orlogsskip, saa viser jeg Dem stedet. Seiler De saa med en slik flaate mot Deres grav, er det ikke min skyld.

Jakob Blank

column2: Destruction
column3: Fordervelse

column2:
Fool that I am, that's what I get for challenging fate. Everyone knows, that if you have escaped from the "flying trader" you are not allowed to relate the story, never!  And I, the unbeliever, even offered to disclose its whereabouts.
Ever since my garrulous stupidity, the once rich Stetin has been plagued by epidemics and crop failures. Pirates lay in wait on every ship that wants to supply the town with the most needed necessities. 
I have brought a great disaster over the only place in this world that still means something to me. Stetin once had a population of over 3500 inhabitants but soon; you won't be able to find it on any map.
Coming generations will remember: Stetin; the lost town, the town that had to perish because of the stupidity of a single person. Oh wretched me! I cannot tell you where the "flying trader" is. It would cause a great misfortune come about.
Go away and come back only when my hometown has been saved!

Jakob Blank
column3:
Tosk som jeg er, slik gaar det naar man utfordrer skjebnen. Alle vet at den som har sluppet unna "Den flygende handelsmann", aldri maa fortelle historien, aldri! Og jeg, den vantro, tilboed til og med aa roepe hvor han er.
Siden min snakkesalige dumhet hjemsoekes det en gang saa rike Stettin av farsotter og uaar. Pirater ligger paa lur etter hvert skip som vil forsyne byen med det aller mest noedvendige.
Jeg har brakt en stor ulykke over det eneste stedet i verden som fortsatt betyr noe for meg. Stettin hadde en gang over 3500 innbyggere, men snart vil De ikke finne den paa noe kart.
Kommende slekter vil huske: Stettin, den fortapte byen, byen som maatte gaa under paa grunn av ett enkelt menneskes dumhet. Ve meg! Jeg kan ikke si Dem hvor "Den flygende handelsmann" er. Det ville bringe stor ulykke.
Gaa Deres vei, og kom foerst igjen naar hjembyen min er reddet!

Jakob Blank

column2: Sad person
column3: Soergelig skikkelse

column2:
Brave Leopold!

You have taken it upon yourself to save this town; condemned to doom? Indeed, the citizens of Stetin deserve nothing less than this, grant asylum to this poor sinner Blank.  He was driven out of Riga in shame and disgrace, which wasn't funny. Stetin opened its door to him because he paid a generous donation into the town treasury, which the fat councillors then put into their own pockets.
Stetin's fatty days are over, and believe me; you can't bring them back even if you tried!

H. Vanderdeeken
column3:
Tapre Leopold!

De har paatatt Dem aa redde denne byen, doemt til undergang? Sannelig fortjener Stettins borgere ikke mindre, de som ga ly til denne stakkars synderen Blank. Han ble jaget ut av Riga med skam og vanaere, og det var ikke til aa le av. Stettin aapnet portene for ham fordi han betalte en raus gave til byens kasse, som de fete raadmennene siden stakk i egne lommer.
Stettins fete aar er forbi, og tro meg: De faar dem ikke tilbake, selv om De proever!

H. Vanderdeeken

column2: Rescue
column3: Redning

column2:
Noble Jantzen!

Saviour of Stetin, you have shown truly great courage in standing by my hometown against the raging storms of fate. Your success has strengthened my decision to tell you my last secret: The position, where you are most likely to meet the  "flying trader" is.

Be careful, and God be with you!

Jakob Blank
column3:
Edle Jantzen!

Stettins redningsmann, De har vist virkelig stort mot ved aa staa min hjemby bi mot skjebnens rasende stormer. Deres suksess har styrket min beslutning om aa fortelle Dem min siste hemmelighet: posisjonen der De med stoerst sannsynlighet moeter "Den flygende handelsmann".

Vaer forsiktig, og Gud vaere med Dem!

Jakob Blank

column2: Musty hulk
column3: Muggen holk

column2:
Dear Sir!

We went to the position marked on the chart and waited there. The wind suddenly became calm and we slowly rode the current. A second ship with ragged sails was being carried by strong currents diagonally towards us. As soon as a light breeze set in, we boarded the ship and examined it carefully.It was just a dilapidated old hulk; in its cargo rooms there were stacks of empty decayed trunks and caskets.
There wasn't a crew on board, nor were there any signs that it had recently been used. We sank the ship according to your orders, and this is my full report.

With nautical greetings,

Captain of the {%s:09}
column3:
Herre!

Vi seilte til posisjonen som var avmerket paa kartet, og ventet der. Plutselig loeyet vinden, og vi drev langsomt med stroemmen. Et annet skip med fillete seil ble av sterke stroemmer foert skraatt mot oss. Saa snart en lett bris satte inn, entret vi skipet og undersoekte det noeye. Det var bare en forfallen gammel holk; i lasterommene sto stabler av tomme, raatne kister og skrin.
Det var ikke noe mannskap om bord og ingen tegn paa at skipet nylig var brukt. Vi senket skipet etter Deres ordre, og dette er min fullstendige rapport.

Med sjoemannshilsen,

Kapteinen paa {%s:09}

column2: Relief
column3: Lettelse

column2:
Brave Jantzen!

I have heard about your meeting with the ghost ship. Because you and your entire crew got away, it would appear that the curse of the "travelling trader" has now at last been broken.  Christian shipping is greatly indebted to you, much more than that however, is that I owe you a great debt of gratitude, then you have removed a dark shadow from my soul.There is a rumour that you would now like to be elected Lord Mayor of Bremen, and put this complacent Vanderdeeken in his place. I would love to be in on it, but freed from this terrible burden, I will now peacefully enter the kingdom of the dead. 

Farewell,

Jakob Blank
column3:
Tapre Jantzen!

Jeg har hoert om Deres moete med spoekelsesskipet. Siden De og hele mannskapet Deres slapp fra det, synes forbannelsen over "Den flygende handelsmann" endelig aa vaere brutt. Den kristne skipsfarten staar i stor gjeld til Dem, men enda mer skylder jeg Dem stor takk, for De har fjernet en moerk skygge fra min sjel. Det ryktes at De naa vil velges til borgermester i Bremen og sette den selvgode Vanderdeeken paa plass. Hvor gjerne jeg ville vaert med, men befridd fra denne forferdelige byrden gaar jeg naa i fred inn i de doedes rike.

Farvel,

Jakob Blank

column2:
Estate of the late Mr Jakob Blank

Mr Jakob Blank died of natural causes at his home in Stetin last night. He leaves no dependents and his recently modified Last Will and Testament declares {%R:04} Leopold Jantzen as sole benefactor.An examination of his estate shows that Mr Blank who lived in poor conditions had change to the amount of 500.000\C.
The full amount will be transferred to you immediately.

Finance Officer, Stetin
{%+:0C}
column3:
Bo etter avdoede herr Jakob Blank

Herr Jakob Blank doede i natt en naturlig doed i sitt hjem i Stettin. Han etterlater seg ingen paaroerende, og hans nylig endrede testamente innsetter {%R:04} Leopold Jantzen som eneste arving. En gjennomgang av boet viser at herr Blank, som levde under fattige kaar, eide summen av 500.000\C.
Hele beloepet overfoeres straks til Dem.

Byens kemner i Stettin
{%+:0C}

column2: Move
column3: Flytting

column2:
Young Sir!

I congratulate you on your latest deeds. The house has been in euphoric mood since the arrival of your latest news. Everyone is busy making last minute preparations for the move to Bremen.
Your plan is the talk of the entire Hanse; there has even been a message from a cousin from Novgorod wishing you good luck.
Indeed, the citizens of Lubeck regret loosing their most prominent Councilor, but everyone hopes that you'll teach the unpopular Vanderdeeken a lesson.

Your obedient servant,

Karl
column3:
Unge herre!

Jeg gratulerer Dem med Deres siste bragder. Huset har vaert i den hoeyeste begeistring siden Deres siste nyheter kom. Alle har det travelt med de siste forberedelsene til flyttingen til Bremen.
Deres plan er paa alles lepper i hele Hansaen; det har til og med kommet et budskap fra en fetter i Novgorod som oensker Dem lykke til.
Riktignok beklager Luebecks borgere aa miste sin fremste raadmann, men alle haaper at De vil gi den upopulaere Vanderdeeken en laerepenge.

Deres lydige tjener,

Karl

column2: Warning
column3: Advarsel

column2:
Now, Master Jantzen!

Have you come to Bremen to offer me your services? Oh no, I hear you wanted to become Lord Mayor in my town. The rabble and its kind are supporting you in this foolish undertaking, as well, what!
I'll say this as a warning: the people, who are now cheering for you, are only driven by their own jealousies. They are jealous of my wealth and my power, but if the truth were known, they admire, and are afraid of me.
They would never speak out publicly against me, and I'll give you this well-meant advice, do the same.
Only because you can sink an old decaying ship, doesn't, in my eyes make you anything more than a "good for nothing", who was brought up in an arrogant way by his father.

H. Vanderdeeken
{%-:00}HV
column3:
Naa, mester Jantzen!

Er De kommet til Bremen for aa tilby meg Deres tjenester? Aa nei, jeg hoerer at De ville bli borgermester i min by. Poebelen og dens like stoetter Dem i dette taapelige foretaket, sannelig!
Jeg sier dette som en advarsel: de som naa hyller Dem, drives bare av sin egen misunnelse. De misunner meg min rikdom og min makt, men i virkeligheten beundrer og frykter de meg.
Aldri ville de offentlig tale mot meg, og jeg gir Dem det velmente raadet aa gjoere det samme.

column2:
Colleague Jantzen,

I am seriously worried about your father's soul. Your father had to pawn his entire future wealth to progress half as much again in his career, and I really wouldn't want to know what sort of crooked business would bring you so quickly forward. 
I hardly believe that the sudden wealth, which you so uninhibitedly display to the public, is earned by honest work. Are you not making the same mistake as once did your father?

H. Vanderdeeken

column3:
Kollega Jantzen,

Jeg er alvorlig bekymret for Deres fars sjel. Deres far maatte pantsette hele sin fremtidige formue for aa komme halvparten saa langt i sin loepebane, og jeg vil virkelig ikke vite hvilke lyssky forretninger som bringer Dem saa raskt fremover.
Jeg tror neppe at den plutselige rikdommen De saa ugenert viser frem offentlig, er tjent ved aerlig arbeid. Begaar De ikke den samme feilen som Deres far en gang?

H. Vanderdeeken

Damn you Jantzen!

That you always have to get involved in things, which you do not wish to understand. Obviously, you have a certain talent for manipulating people and have robbed me of making a beautiful speech, Dear Lord Mayor.

You may now be laughing maliciously and in triumph but I'll get my own back. Sooner or later, we'll meet again, I can already promise you that.

De ler kanskje naa skadefro og triumferende, men jeg skal faa min hevn. Foer eller siden moetes vi igjen, det kan jeg allerede love Dem.

Dear Lord Mayor Jantzen!

A letter arrived here sometime ago from Stetin; it was addressed to " Lord Mayor Jantzen of Bremen". We assumed it was a mistake and sent it back. But it was sent again from Stetin and then it became forgotten, until I, on the occasion of your taking over office as Lord Mayor, remembered it. It appears that letter must have been addressed to you and that we may deliver it, now that you are lord Mayor.

The Post Office Bremen.
column3:
Kjaere borgermester Jantzen!

For en tid siden kom det et brev hit fra Stettin; det var adressert til "borgermester Jantzen i Bremen". Vi trodde det var en feil og sendte det tilbake. Men det ble sendt paa nytt fra Stettin og gikk siden i glemmeboken, til jeg husket det i anledning Deres tiltredelse som borgermester. Det ser ut til at brevet var stilet til Dem, og at vi kan levere det, naa som De er borgermester.

Posthuset i Bremen.

\f1_Here the letter kept for you.
\f3_

\rStetin, {%D:11}
\lI poor sinner!

A little while ago, one of your sailors came to the bed in which I will die shortly. He was on the trip to the ghost ship and should now relate the events in every single detail to me. From his story, and to my horror, I realised that you were not personally there.
This naturally changes every thing; then with your father's money in your pocket you would have to have seen the ghost ship. I am taking on double and triple burden of guilt on myself, to warn you with this letter, at least, of the imminent disaster.

At our last meeting you mentioned that you were the Lord Mayor of Bremen. That must be the quickest way for this letter reach you, and then you at least, can save your soul. However one thing at a time:
I did not tell you the whole truth about the "flying trader" and my meeting with the ghost ship.

Namely, if he who is of a pure conscience and without ambitions of profit, meets the ghost ship, he will see nothing more in it than a over a hundred year old weather beaten ship and is at first, not in any danger.
However, he who goes on board with greed in his heart, or has part of the treasure of the ghost ship in his moneybag, will be met by an appearance of the greedy trader and a deal suggested. He, who agrees, gets a share of the treasure but sells the souls of all honourable seamen on board for it.
The treasure is enchanted and multiplies itself almost automatically, the curse however, is this; to strive to get back to its master and in the end brings nothing but misfortune for the illegal owner.

Your father's business was not doing well at the time and he had fallen in love with a beautiful girl in Lubeck, whose father did want anything to do with a poor man's wedding. I had lost a lot of money gambling, and so we were sitting a tavern in Bremen, thinking about what to do before this unfortunate journey, when a stranger came to our table. He knew all about our situation and offered us his support. What he demanded for it was nothing less than a fair share of our future wealth. We agreed because we didn't have anything to lose, and he said that; on our next journey a ship with which we could make the deal of our lives would meet us.
I do not need to describe the details of coming events, I'm sure you can already guess them. We sold "Morning Greetings" to the "flying trader" and landed ashore with a dinghy full of gold.
From now on we seem to have nothing but luck, your father got his girl and quickly climbed the career ladder in Lubeck. I paid off my debts and above that won large sums until one day the stranger turned up again. At first, he demanded your father's sweet little baby daughter. Then he came to me: I refused to pay the price he demanded from me and was driven as a common criminal from my then hometown. Since then I have been, once or twice, on the run and lost contact with your father as a result. It was only in Stetin that I more or less returned to a normal life, but I never touched any of the money, which I still had. And now I'll have to die with sins because I never told you the whole truth in time. I can only advice you to hide all your father's money and that which I will leave you for safekeeping. Do not touch it, under no circumstances should use it as an investment, otherwise the curse of the  "flying trader" will be on you, and you'll never find peace in this world.

Farewell,

Jakob Blank
column3:
\f1_Her er brevet som ble oppbevart til Dem.
\f3_

\rStettin, {%D:11}
\lJeg arme synder!

For kort tid siden kom en av Deres matroser til sengen der jeg snart skal doe. Han var med paa reisen til spoekelsesskipet og skulle naa fortelle meg hendelsene i alle detaljer. Av beretningen hans forsto jeg til min forferdelse at De ikke selv var med.
Det endrer naturligvis alt, for med Deres fars penger i lommen skulle De ellers ha sett spoekelsesskipet. Jeg tar paa meg dobbel og tredobbel skyld og vil med dette brevet i det minste advare Dem mot den forestaaende ulykken.

Ved vaart siste moete nevnte De at De er borgermester i Bremen. Der maa dette brevet naa Dem raskest, og da kan i det minste De redde Deres sjel. Men én ting om gangen:
Jeg fortalte ikke hele sannheten om "Den flygende handelsmann" og mitt moete med spoekelsesskipet.

Den som nemlig med ren samvittighet og uten vinnings hensikt moeter spoekelsesskipet, ser ikke annet i det enn et skip som er vaerbitt gjennom aarhundrer, og er i begynnelsen ikke i fare.
Men den som gaar om bord med graadighet i hjertet, eller baerer en del av spoekelsesskipets skatt i pungen, moeter et syn av den graadige handelsmannen, som foreslaar en handel. Den som slaar til, faar en del av skatten, men selger til gjengjeld sjelene til alle hederlige sjoefolk om bord.
Skatten er forhekset og formerer seg nesten av seg selv, men forbannelsen er at den streber tilbake til sin herre og til slutt ikke bringer den urettmessige eieren annet enn ulykke.

Deres fars forretninger gikk ikke godt den gang, og han hadde forelsket seg i en vakker pike i Luebeck, hvis far ikke ville vite av noe fattig bryllup. Jeg hadde tapt mye penger paa spill, og saa satt vi foer denne ulykkelige reisen og raadslo paa et vertshus i Bremen, da en fremmed kom bort til bordet vaart. Han visste alt om vaar noed og tilboed sin stoette. Det han krevde for den, var ikke annet enn en rimelig andel av vaar fremtidige rikdom. Vi slo til, siden vi ikke hadde noe aa tape, og han sa at vi paa neste reise ville moete et skip som vi kunne gjoere vaart livs handel med.
Jeg trenger ikke beskrive detaljene i det som fulgte; De gjetter dem sikkert allerede. Vi solgte "Morgenhilsen" til "Den flygende handelsmann" og naadde fastlandet med en jolle full av gull.
Fra da av syntes lykken aa smile til oss: Deres far fikk sin pike og gjorde raskt karriere i Luebeck. Jeg betalte min gjeld og vant attpaatil store summer, til den fremmede en dag dukket opp igjen. Foerst krevde han av Deres far hans soete lille datter. Saa kom han til meg: jeg nektet aa betale prisen han krevde, og ble jaget som en simpel forbryter ut av min davaerende hjemby. Siden har jeg gang paa gang vaert paa flukt og mistet derved kontakten med Deres far. Foerst i Stettin fant jeg igjen et noenlunde normalt liv, men pengene jeg hadde igjen, roerte jeg aldri. Og naa maa jeg doe med synder, fordi jeg ikke i tide fortalte Dem hele sannheten. Jeg kan bare raade Dem til aa gjemme alle Deres fars penger og det jeg etterlater Dem til oppbevaring. Roer dem ikke, og bruk dem under ingen omstendigheter til aa formere dem, ellers rammer "Den flygende handelsmanns" forbannelse Dem, og De vil aldri finne fred i denne verden.

Farvel,

Jakob Blank
