column2: Mission objective
column3: Oppdragets maal

column2:
You now have a year to rise from shopkeeper to trader.

Luebeck's strengths lie in fishing and the production of iron goods. Wood and bricks are also produced there, so you shouldn't have any problems constructing new buildings.

On the other hand, Luebeck only produces a little grain and no beer at all. So first of all, you should concentrate on getting beer from Stettin or Gdansk. You can also go to Hamburg or Bremen, but they are both further away.

Gdansk is always short of iron goods and sometimes of fish too. Stettin also urgently needs iron goods.

Make sure that you don't pay too much for the goods. The limits are around 450\C for fish, 450\C for iron goods and 50\C for beer.
column3:
De har naa ett aar paa aa avansere fra kremmer til handelsmann.

Luebecks styrke ligger i fisket og fremstillingen av jernvarer. Der fremstilles ogsaa toemmer og murstein, saa De boer ikke faa problemer med aa reise nye bygninger.

Til gjengjeld fremstiller Luebeck bare litt korn og ikke noe oel i det hele tatt. Konsentrer Dem derfor foerst om aa skaffe oel fra Stettin eller Gdansk. De kan ogsaa dra til Hamburg eller Bremen, men de ligger begge lenger unna.

Gdansk mangler alltid jernvarer og av og til ogsaa fisk. Ogsaa Stettin trenger saart jernvarer.

Soerg for at De ikke betaler for mye for varene. Grensene ligger omkring 450\C for fisk, 450\C for jernvarer og 50\C for oel.

column2:
Because trade in iron goods is important, you should ensure that there is always enough pig iron in Luebeck, as this raw material cannot be produced here.
This is however produced in Oslo, for instance. This town is also an appreciative buyer of grain, iron goods and beer.

However, you should always sell as many goods to Luebeck as possible, as this is the quickest way to increase your recognition, so that your advancement to trader status will not take too long.

Incidentally, don't start producing any buildings or ships yet. We can come back to that once you have achieved trader status.
column3:
Siden handelen med jernvarer er viktig, boer De soerge for at det alltid finnes nok raajern i Luebeck, for dette raastoffet kan ikke fremstilles her.
Det fremstilles derimot for eksempel i Oslo. Den byen kjoeper ogsaa gjerne korn, jernvarer og oel.

Selg likevel alltid saa mange varer som mulig til Luebeck, for det er den raskeste maaten aa oeke Deres anseelse paa, saa forfremmelsen til handelsmann ikke tar for lang tid.

Begynn forresten ikke aa bygge bygninger eller skip ennaa. Det kommer vi tilbake til naar De er blitt handelsmann.

column2:
Now you must make it from trader to merchant status. You have 6 months to do this. Besides trading, you should now build facilities and town houses in your home town.

As you know, Luebeck's strengths are fishing and the manufacture of iron goods. Start by building a facility for each of these industries. You may have to get the raw building materials for these from other towns. But you should only construct one of each building to start with, as you will also have to find buyers for your goods.

Building facilities brings you two advantages besides trade: firstly, your reputation grows with every worker that you employ. Secondly, creating new workplaces draws new citizens into the town. This increases demand and you can sell more goods.

If your facilities are to fill up with workers quickly, the poor townspeople must at the very least be contented. You should therefore continue to take good care of the town. The workers also need somewhere to live. If existing town houses are too overcrowded, you should build a new one.
column3:
Naa maa De avansere fra handelsmann til kjoepmann. De har 6 maaneder paa det. I tillegg til handelen boer De naa bygge verksteder og borgerhus i hjembyen.

Som De vet, ligger Luebecks styrke i fisket og fremstillingen av jernvarer. Begynn med aa bygge et verksted for hver av disse naeringene. Kanskje maa De hente byggematerialene fra andre byer. Men bygg til aa begynne med bare én bygning av hvert slag, for De maa ogsaa finne kjoepere til varene Deres.

Verksteder gir Dem to fordeler i tillegg til handelen: for det foerste vokser Deres rykte med hver arbeider De ansetter. For det andre trekker nye arbeidsplasser nye borgere til byen. Det oeker etterspoerselen, og De kan selge flere varer.

Skal verkstedene Deres raskt fylles med arbeidere, maa byens fattige i det minste vaere fornoeyde. Fortsett derfor aa soerge godt for byen. Arbeiderne trenger ogsaa et sted aa bo. Er de eksisterende husene overfylte, boer De bygge et nytt.

column2:
Bear in mind that your facilities need raw materials. These must be available from your trading office.

If you have a trading office manager, he can buy in the raw materials when the town needs them. You don't need to worry about this at the moment though, especially since a manager also costs money.

To see which raw materials your facilities need, click on a facility once it is completed. You can also find out from your trading office what all of your facilities in the town need.
column3:
Husk at verkstedene Deres trenger raavarer. De maa vaere tilgjengelige i Deres kontor.

Har De en kontorforvalter, kan han kjoepe inn raavarene naar byen trenger dem. Det trenger De likevel ikke bekymre Dem for naa, saerlig siden en forvalter ogsaa koster penger.

For aa se hvilke raavarer verkstedene Deres trenger, klikker De paa et verksted naar det er ferdig. I Deres kontor kan De ogsaa se hva alle verkstedene Deres i byen trenger.

column2:
To become a merchant, you naturally need to acquire even greater recognition and amass considerable wealth. You should concentrate on cloth, wine and meat for the richer inhabitants of your home town. Try adding furs too - you will find them in the east.

If you should ever happen to come across spices, buy them! They are another much sought-after product with the rich citizens of Luebeck.
column3:
For aa bli kjoepmann trenger De naturligvis enda stoerre anseelse og en betydelig formue. Konsentrer Dem om klede, vin og kjoett til de rikere innbyggerne i hjembyen. Proev ogsaa med skinn - dem finner De i oest.

Skulle De noen gang komme over krydder, saa kjoep det! Det er en annen svaert ettertraktet vare blant Luebecks rike borgere.

column2:
To transport the manufactured goods out of the town more efficiently, you should own at least one more ship. Commission a snaikka or crayer from the Luebeck shipyard.

Use your Luebeck shipyard as often as possible - including for repairs - because the more orders it gets, the better the ships will be that are built there.
column3:
For aa frakte de fremstilte varene ut av byen mer effektivt boer De eie minst ett skip til. Bestill en schnigge eller en kraier hos verftet i Luebeck.

Bruk verftet i Luebeck saa ofte som mulig - ogsaa til reparasjoner - for jo flere bestillinger det faar, desto bedre blir skipene som bygges der.

column2: All you need to advance from merchant to long distance merchant is a bit more recognition and some extra wealth. You must also be a member of the guild - which is sure to increase your reputation.\nOnce again, you have 6 months to complete your rise in status.\n
column3: Alt De trenger for aa avansere fra kjoepmann til fjernhandelsmann, er litt mer anseelse og litt ekstra formue. De maa ogsaa vaere medlem av gildet - noe som sikkert vil oeke Deres rykte.\nIgjen har De 6 maaneder paa forfremmelsen.\n

column2:
Bear in mind that your wealth includes not only your cash, but also facilities, town houses, ships and stored goods. However, any debts that you have with the moneylender are deducted.

If living space becomes limited in Luebeck, you should quickly build an appropriate number of town houses, as every tenant will bring you - just like every worker that you employ - additional recognition amongst the tenants. If you are too slow, your competitors, or the town itself may build town houses, in which case you will find it harder to fill your own. As the town houses also cost you weekly land taxes, they must be adequately populated to ensure that you can make a profit. The utilisation rate for half-timbered houses must therefore be over 70{%%:00}, while the utilisation rate for other houses must be at least 50{%%:00}.
column3:
Husk at formuen Deres ikke bare omfatter rede penger, men ogsaa verksteder, borgerhus, skip og lagrede varer. Gjeld hos laangiveren trekkes likevel fra.

Blir boligplassen knapp i Luebeck, boer De raskt bygge et passende antall borgerhus, for hver leieboer gir Dem - akkurat som hver arbeider De ansetter - ekstra anseelse blant leieboerne. Er De for langsom, kan konkurrentene Deres eller byen selv bygge borgerhus, og da blir det vanskeligere aa fylle Deres egne. Siden borgerhusene ogsaa koster Dem ukentlig grunnskatt, maa de vaere tilstrekkelig bebodd for at De skal tjene penger. Belegget i bindingsverkshus maa derfor vaere over 70{%%:00}, i andre hus minst 50{%%:00}.

column2: Have you joined the Luebeck Guild yet? You must be a member of a guild before you can attain the status of long distance merchant or higher.\nBy the way, the guild entry fee increases as you become wealthier. It also decreases as your reputation in the town grows.\n
column3: Har De allerede gaatt inn i gildet i Luebeck? De maa vaere medlem av et gilde foer De kan naa fjernhandelsmanns rang eller hoeyere.\nForresten stiger gildets innskudd jo rikere De blir. Det synker ogsaa etter hvert som Deres rykte i byen vokser.\n

column2:
You must acquire a considerable increase in reputation with all the town's inhabitants within a year, if you are to advance to councillor status. As you also need to be much wealthier, you should invest as much as possible in your hometown, as investments increase your wealth and enhance your reputation.
Double or treble your production in Luebeck and build town houses in plenty of time, so that the new workers and their families can become your tenants. 
As your production increases, you also need to build new ships, so that the goods being produced can be transported.
column3:
De maa innen ett aar oeke Deres rykte betydelig blant alle byens innbyggere for aa bli raadmann. Siden De ogsaa maa bli mye rikere, boer De investere saa mye som mulig i hjembyen, for investeringer oeker formuen og hever Deres rykte.
Doble eller tredoble produksjonen i Luebeck, og bygg borgerhus i god tid, saa de nye arbeiderne og familiene deres kan bli Deres leieboere.
Etter hvert som produksjonen oeker, trenger De ogsaa nye skip, saa de fremstilte varene kan fraktes.

column2:
Here are a couple more hints that may help you to improve your reputation.
Basically, all you need to know is that everything you do for your home town means a better reputation. If you spend money on the church or the public bath, your reputation increases. If you issue a loan or construct buildings and facilities, it increases again. It can also benefit from family, organisation of a celebration, a large fortune or the provision of guard ships. 
But it can also deteriorate if, for example, a criminal offence comes to light, if you demolish facilities or if you demand a high interest rate when extending a loan.
Incidentally, your recognition can also increase following a successful expedition, as all Hansa towns benefit from this. Just undertake an expedition every now and again, and discover new places to sell your wares.
column3:
Her er et par raad til som kan hjelpe Dem med aa bedre Deres rykte.
I bunn og grunn trenger De bare aa vite at alt De gjoer for hjembyen, betyr bedre rykte. Bruker De penger paa kirken eller det offentlige badet, stiger Deres rykte. Gir De et laan eller bygger bygninger og verksteder, stiger det igjen. Ogsaa familien, aa holde en fest, en stor formue eller aa stille vaktskip til raadighet gagner det.
Men det kan ogsaa forverres om for eksempel en forbrytelse kommer for dagen, om De river verksteder, eller om De krever hoey rente naar De gir et laan.
Deres anseelse kan forresten ogsaa vokse etter en vellykket ekspedisjon, for alle hansabyer nyter godt av den. Gjennomfoer derfor en ekspedisjon av og til, og oppdag nye steder aa avsette varene Deres.

column2:
To enable you to gain even more profit from trade, you should build a trading office in as many other towns as possible and produce goods there. It isn't always cheaper to produce goods yourself than to buy them at a low price. But by producing goods yourself, you can be sure of a constant price and a consistent quantity. This is particularly useful for setting up trade routes, to ensure a continuous supply to your home town, for example, or to exchange your own goods between two or more trading offices.
But be careful how you select your facilities. Think about which goods the towns are still likely to need in the future. Because if you produce more than can be used, the goods will stock pile in the towns and the price (and therefore your profit) will decrease in the long run.
column3:
For aa faa enda mer ut av handelen boer De bygge et kontor i saa mange andre byer som mulig og fremstille varer der. Det er ikke alltid billigere aa fremstille selv enn aa kjoepe billig. Men ved aa fremstille selv er De sikret en fast pris og en jevn mengde. Det er saerlig nyttig naar De setter opp handelsruter, for eksempel for stadig aa forsyne hjembyen eller utveksle egne varer mellom to eller flere kontorer.
Men vaer noeye med valget av verksteder. Tenk over hvilke varer byene sannsynligvis fortsatt vil trenge i fremtiden. For fremstiller De mer enn som kan brukes, hoper varene seg opp i byene, og prisen (og dermed fortjenesten Deres) synker i det lange loep.

column2:
To enable you to gain even more profit from trade, you should build a trading office in as many other towns as possible and produce goods there. It isn't always cheaper to produce goods yourself than to buy them at a low price. But by producing goods yourself, you can be sure of a constant price and a consistent quantity. This is particularly useful for setting up trade routes, to ensure a continuous supply to your home town, for example, or to exchange your own goods between two or more trading offices.
But be careful how you select your facilities. Think about which goods the towns are still likely to need in the future. Because if you produce more than can be used, the goods will mount up in the towns and the price (and therefore your profit) will decrease over time. 
If particular goods that you are producing are no longer profitable, don't hesitate about shutting them down or demolishing the relevant facility.
column3:
For aa faa enda mer ut av handelen boer De bygge et kontor i saa mange andre byer som mulig og fremstille varer der. Det er ikke alltid billigere aa fremstille selv enn aa kjoepe billig. Men ved aa fremstille selv er De sikret en fast pris og en jevn mengde. Det er saerlig nyttig naar De setter opp handelsruter, for eksempel for stadig aa forsyne hjembyen eller utveksle egne varer mellom to eller flere kontorer.
Men vaer noeye med valget av verksteder. Tenk over hvilke varer byene sannsynligvis fortsatt vil trenge i fremtiden. For fremstiller De mer enn som kan brukes, hoper varene seg opp i byene, og prisen (og dermed fortjenesten Deres) synker med tiden.
Er visse varer De fremstiller, ikke lenger loennsomme, saa noel ikke med aa stanse produksjonen eller rive det aktuelle verkstedet.

column2: The main thing you need to focus on is achieving popularity in your home town, even when rising to the rank of Patrician. Only when you have achieved this step will you be able to aim for the position of Lord Mayor.
column3: Det viktigste er at De vinner popularitet i hjembyen, ogsaa for aa naa patrisiers rang. Foerst naar De har tatt det steget, kan De strebe etter borgermesterembetet.

column2:
You're on the right track!
But if you want to become a trader, you will also have to look after the rich citizens in Luebeck. These folk aren't that bothered about beer and grain so you should try to make them happier with meat, wine and cloth.
 
You can get meat in Aalborg and Bergen. But make sure that Aalborg has enough salt, otherwise no meat can be produced there. You can take some salt with you from Luebeck.

You can get wine from Cologne. The citizens there could do with some fish and beer.

There is plenty of cloth available in Visby. Find out what they need there.
column3:
De er paa rett vei!
Men vil De bli handelsmann, maa De ogsaa ta Dem av de rike borgerne i Luebeck. Det folket bryr seg ikke stort om oel og korn, saa proev aa gjoere dem mer fornoeyde med kjoett, vin og klede.
 
Kjoett faar De i Aalborg og Bergen. Men soerg for at Aalborg har nok salt, ellers kan det ikke fremstilles kjoett der. De kan ta med litt salt fra Luebeck.

Vin faar De fra Cologne. Borgerne der kunne godt trenge litt fisk og oel.

I Visby finnes det klede i overflod. Finn ut hva man trenger der.

column2:
Normally, your reputation in a town increases whenever you supply goods to the town. However, this only applies if the town actually needs that particular product. You can tell if a product is no longer required when the sales price is very close to the purchase price. 

Incidentally, you can also lose reputation in a town by buying up scarce goods. So don't do this in your home town!
column3:
Vanligvis vokser Deres rykte i en by hver gang De leverer varer dit. Det gjelder likevel bare hvis byen virkelig trenger akkurat den varen. De kan se at en vare ikke lenger trengs naar salgsprisen ligger svaert naer innkjoepsprisen.

De kan forresten ogsaa miste anseelse i en by ved aa kjoepe opp knappe varer. Gjoer altsaa ikke det i hjembyen Deres!

column2: You will notice little product icons against the different towns on the sea map. These indicate which goods are most urgently required.\nBe careful: this information takes a while to reach you, so an icon may already be out of date by the time you arrive in the town. If you want to use these icons to make extra profit, you must therefore concentrate your efforts on the towns in the area immediately surrounding Luebeck.\n
column3: De vil se smaa varesymboler ved de ulike byene paa sjoekartet. De viser hvilke varer det er mest akutt behov for.\nVaer forsiktig: disse opplysningene bruker en stund paa aa naa Dem, saa et symbol kan allerede vaere utdatert naar De kommer til byen. Vil De bruke symbolene til ekstra fortjeneste, maa De derfor konsentrere innsatsen om byene i Luebecks umiddelbare naerhet.\n

column2: Bear in mind that your rank is bestowed on you by your home town, so the main thing is therefore that you are well known in this town. Your current rank is displayed in your trading office overview.\n\n
column3: Husk at Deres rang tildeles Dem av hjembyen, saa det viktigste er at De er godt kjent der. Deres naavaerende rang vises i oversikten over Deres kontor.\n\n

column2: Winter is drawing near! Buy grain and beer and store it in your trading office, so that you can still provide for your home town in winter and gain a good reputation with the citizens.
column3: Vinteren naermer seg! Kjoep korn og oel og lagre det i Deres kontor, saa De ogsaa om vinteren kan forsyne hjembyen og vinne et godt rykte blant borgerne.

column2:
My dearest son,

You are now old enough to follow in my footsteps, but you must gain your own experiences first.

I spent some happy times roaming the entire Hanseatic region as a free trader and captain of a glorious Snaikka, before settling down in {%t:01} to fulfil my political commitments and marry your mother. I would like you to follow in my footsteps and be admitted to the Hanseatic League on your own merits. As start-up capital, You will recieved a Snaikka, a Crayer, and a trading office in {%t:01} - so that we might see each other once in a while - and some cash. This should make it easy for you to achieve the rank of trader.

Your loving father, 

Georg Jantzen
{%-:00}GJ
column3:
Min kjaereste soenn,

Naa er du gammel nok til aa foelge i mine fotspor, men foerst maa du skaffe deg egen erfaring.

Jeg hadde lykkelige tider da jeg reiste rundt i hele Hansaens omraade som fri handelsmann og kaptein paa en prektig schnigge, foer jeg slo meg ned i {%t:01} for aa oppfylle mine politiske forpliktelser og gifte meg med din mor. Jeg vil at du skal foelge i mine fotspor og bli tatt opp i Hansaen paa egne fortjenester. Som startkapital faar du en schnigge, en kraier og et kontor i {%t:01} - saa vi kan se hverandre av og til - samt litt rede penger. Det boer gjoere det lett for deg aa naa handelsmanns rang.

Din kjaerlige far,

Georg Jantzen
{%-:00}GJ

column2: Gone
column3: Borte

column2:
My dearest son,

You have certainly had a splendid education, as you were fortunate enough to be taught by the brightest brains in Europe. But you have barely left dry land so far.
So let me give you some good advice as you go on your way: be as much on your guard against the "Flying Trader" as you would against the Kobold! There are many dangers awaiting you on the open seas, but this ghost ship is the Devil's own spawn.

May God protect you.
P. S. Your mother is worried about you, so please don't be too bold in your youthful recklessness!

Georg Jantzen
{%-:00}GJ
column3:
Min kjaereste soenn,

Du har sannelig faatt en glimrende oppdragelse, siden du var saa heldig aa bli undervist av Europas klokeste hoder. Men hittil har du knapt forlatt fast grunn.
La meg derfor gi deg et godt raad paa veien: vaer like mye paa vakt mot "Den flygende handelsmann" som mot nissen! Mange farer venter deg paa det aapne hav, men dette spoekelsesskipet er djevelens eget avkom.

Gud bevare deg.
P.S. Din mor er bekymret for deg, saa vaer ikke for dristig i ditt ungdommelige overmot!

Georg Jantzen
{%-:00}GJ

column2:
My dearest son,

I am delighted to see how your business is flourishing. If you carry on like this, you will easily make it to trader and much more besides.

But you mustn't think only of your own financial gain. You should also tend to the needs of the people in the towns you are trading with. Remember: wealth can make you lonely!

However, I have a sad reason for writing to you today. Your mother is ill. She has been confined to bed with a high fever for several days, and even the Hanseatic League's very best doctors have no idea which rare disease she has. I have had a physician from Florence sent for; I only hope he will get here in time!

Love from your mother and me, and take care.

Georg Jantzen
{%-:00}GJ
column3:
Min kjaereste soenn,

Det gleder meg aa se hvor godt forretningene dine blomstrer. Fortsetter du slik, blir du lett handelsmann og mye mer.

Men du maa ikke bare tenke paa din egen vinning. Du boer ogsaa ta vare paa behovene til folket i byene du handler med. Husk: rikdom kan gjoere ensom!

Men i dag skriver jeg av en soergelig grunn. Din mor er syk. Hun har ligget til sengs med hoey feber i flere dager, og selv Hansaens aller beste leger aner ikke hvilken sjelden sykdom hun har. Jeg har sendt bud etter en lege fra Firenze; jeg haaper bare han kommer i tide!

Kjaerlig hilsen fra din mor og meg, og ta vare paa deg selv.

Georg Jantzen
{%-:00}GJ

column2:
My dearest son,

Why must joy and sorrow always go together? I had barely shown the mayor out, who had dropped by to tell me about your appointment as trader, when Master Ardovini summoned me. - This is the famous physician that I told you about in my last letter. He arrived in {%t:01} two weeks ago, but even he was unable to treat your mother's mysterious illness.
She died suddenly three days ago, although she had been in a stable condition for a long time and we were beginning to nurture hopes of her recovery. Her body is to be laid to rest in the {%t:01} crypt next Sunday, and I am now starting to feel the ravages of time eating away at me too.

Please be assured of my congratulations on your rapid advancement, in spite of this distressing news!

Your loving father,

Georg Jantzen
{%-:00}GJ
column3:
Min kjaereste soenn,

Hvorfor maa glede og sorg alltid foelges ad? Knapt hadde jeg fulgt ut borgermesteren, som hadde stukket innom for aa fortelle om din utnevnelse til handelsmann, foer mester Ardovini lot meg kalle. - Det er den beroemte legen jeg skrev om i mitt forrige brev. Han kom til {%t:01} for to uker siden, men selv ikke han kunne behandle din mors gaatefulle sykdom.
Hun doede plutselig for tre dager siden, selv om tilstanden hennes lenge hadde vaert stabil og vi hadde begynt aa naere haap om bedring. Hennes legeme skal gravlegges i krypten i {%t:01} paa soendag, og naa begynner ogsaa jeg aa kjenne tidens tann gnage paa meg.

Ta tross disse triste nyhetene imot min gratulasjon med din raske forfremmelse!

Din kjaerlige far,

Georg Jantzen
{%-:00}GJ

column2: Long Distance Merchant
column3: Fjernhandelsmann

column2:
Dear Leopold,

It is now barely a week since I last wrote to you. I buried your mother yesterday. Now you are all I have left.

May God help my wicked soul, so that I may not lose you as well! You are a cautious trader, and I am sure that you will not disappoint me. I have enclosed 50,000\C with this letter, to help your career advance more quickly.

Once you have achieved the rank of long distance merchant, I wish to entrust you with a secret that has weighed heavy on my mind for many years. Don't ask me about it, as I cannot tell you any more just yet, at least not until I'm sure... No! Away with you, I told him I wouldn't reveal it...


\f1_Young Sir,

Your father has asked me to deliver this letter to you. My mistress's death has hit him so hard that he sometimes seems to be delirious in his waking hours.
However, he already seems to be quite a lot better, so there is no need for you to worry about him.

On behalf of my benevolent master Georg Jantzen,

Your most obedient servant,

\f3_Karl
column3:
Kjaere Leopold,

Det er knapt en uke siden jeg sist skrev til deg. I gaar begravde jeg din mor. Naa er du alt jeg har igjen.

Maatte Gud hjelpe min syndige sjel, saa jeg ikke mister deg ogsaa! Du er en forsiktig handelsmann, og jeg er sikker paa at du ikke skuffer meg. Jeg har lagt ved 50.000\C i dette brevet, saa loepebanen din kan gaa fortere fremover.

Naar du har naadd fjernhandelsmanns rang, vil jeg betro deg en hemmelighet som i mange aar har tynget mitt sinn. Spoer meg ikke om den, jeg kan ikke si mer ennaa, i hvert fall ikke foer jeg er sikker... Nei! Vekk med deg, jeg sa jo til ham at jeg ikke skulle roepe det...


\f1_Unge herre,

Deres far har bedt meg overbringe Dem dette brevet. Min frues doed har rammet ham saa hardt at han av og til synes aa snakke i oerska, selv i vaaken tilstand.
Han synes likevel allerede aa ha det en god del bedre, saa De trenger ikke bekymre Dem for ham.

Paa vegne av min velvillige herre Georg Jantzen,

Deres ydmykeste tjener,

\f3_Karl

column2:
My dearest Son,

I must apologise for my last letter. The worry of the last few weeks weighed heavily on my mind. I am after all, not getting any younger. You, however, have your whole life ahead of you. And although you may not wish to waste any time thinking about this particular subject at the moment, I would like to give you some advice all the same.

I am talking about marriage, and sharing the joys of wedded bliss with a loving bride. My advice is as follows: do look for a kindly, charitable woman, one who is generous to the poor. That will be good for your social reputation and for the salvation of your soul, and even the Kobold will also show you mercy.

May God protect you!

Georg Jantzen
{%-:00}GJ
column3:
Min kjaereste soenn,

Jeg maa be om unnskyldning for mitt forrige brev. De siste ukenes bekymringer tynget meg tungt. Jeg blir jo ikke yngre. Du derimot har hele livet foran deg. Og selv om du kanskje ikke vil kaste bort tid paa aa tenke paa akkurat dette emnet naa, vil jeg likevel gi deg et raad.

Jeg snakker om ekteskapet, og om aa dele ekteskapets gleder med en kjaerlig brud. Mitt raad lyder: soek en godhjertet, barmhjertig kvinne, som er raus mot de fattige. Det vil vaere godt for ditt rykte og for din sjels frelse, og selv nissen vil vise deg naade.

Gud bevare deg!

Georg Jantzen
{%-:00}GJ

column2: Worries
column3: Bekymringer

column2:
Young sir,

I am very worried about your father. In recent nights, he has been suddenly awakend from terrible dreams with increasing frequency and has been shouting for your dear departed mother and for the priest like a man possessed.
He has had nightmares occasionally before, of course, but never this bad.

He is also refusing to leave the house or to let anybody other than the priest in. He has even decreed that you may only be allowed into the house if you have achieved the title of long distance merchant. In his current state of mind, I would not put it past him to throw you out of the house if you did not have this title.

I am writing you this letter without his knowledge and beg you, if you are able to satisfy his wishes, to come and see your father soon.

Your most obedient servant,

Karl
column3:
Unge herre,

Jeg er svaert bekymret for Deres far. De siste nettene har han stadig oftere braatt blitt vekket av forferdelige droemmer og ropt som en besatt paa Deres kjaere avdoede mor og paa presten.
Selvsagt har han hatt mareritt av og til foer, men aldri saa ille.

Han nekter ogsaa aa forlate huset eller slippe inn andre enn presten. Han har til og med bestemt at De bare faar slippe inn hvis De har oppnaadd tittelen fjernhandelsmann. I hans naavaerende sinnstilstand ville det ikke forundre meg om han kastet Dem ut hvis De ikke hadde denne tittelen.

Jeg skriver dette brevet uten hans viten og ber Dem om, hvis De kan oppfylle hans oenske, snart aa komme til Deres far.

Deres ydmykeste tjener,

Karl

column2: Father's Death
column3: Farens doed

column2:
Young Sir,

It is my sad duty to report a tragic event to you. Last night, your father died. His aging heart was unable to cope with the constant agitation any more, and he had not had a restful night's sleep for weeks.
What a cruel twist of fate, just before his dearest wish came true and you were about to come before him as a travelling merchant.
At least your father will have a burial fitting to his position. The news of his death is spreading through the town like wildfire and the citizens of {%t:01} are remembering the good deeds that he performed for the town. And anyone who was not alive to witness the way {%t:01} visibly blossomed while he was mayor is now being regaled with the story at every street corner.
Once again, your family's name is on everybody's lips, unlike before, when your father was only remembered by very few people who had relied on his support for their own careers. I wouldn't be surprised if some of this attention is to your advantage as well.

Your most obedient servant,

Karl
column3:
Unge herre,

Det er min soergelige plikt aa meddele Dem en tragisk hendelse. I natt doede Deres far. Hans aldrende hjerte klarte ikke lenger den stadige uroen, og han hadde ikke faatt en rolig natts soevn paa ukevis.
For et grusomt skjebnens lune, like foer hans kjaereste oenske skulle gaa i oppfyllelse og De skulle tre frem for ham som reisende kjoepmann.
I det minste faar Deres far en begravelse som soemmer seg for hans stilling. Nyheten om hans doed sprer seg som ild i toert gress gjennom byen, og borgerne i {%t:01} minnes de gode gjerningene han gjorde for byen. Og den som ikke selv saa hvordan {%t:01} synlig blomstret mens han var borgermester, faar naa historien fortalt paa hvert gatehjoerne.
Igjen er Deres slekts navn paa alles lepper, i motsetning til foer, da Deres far bare ble husket av de faa som hadde stolt paa hans stoette i sine egne loepebaner. Det ville ikke forundre meg om noe av denne oppmerksomheten ogsaa kommer Dem til gode.

Deres ydmykeste tjener,

Karl

column2:
Young Sir,

My heartfelt congratulations on your rapid advancement. Your father's affairs are progressing normally. After the deeply moving funeral, attended by the whole of {%t:01}, the notaries, court ushers and other officials are now moving in to deal with your father's estate. I shall keep you informed about any developments.

However, I would like to tell you what I know about your father's secret, which he has now taken with him to the grave. I do not think that he would object, now that you are a recognised long distance merchant.
Unfortunately, all I can tell you is that it must have had something to do with a 'Flying Trader', as your father always mumbled about that in his sleep. When I used to take a glass of wine to him in his study late at night, he was sometimes already asleep on the couch, tossing and turning anxiously. It was on one of those occasions that I caught this name.
His nightmares must have originated from an experience that he had at sea during his youth. Your father kept in touch with one of his colleagues from that time for many years. I may be able to find out where he lives. I will write to you again once I have more news.

Your most obedient servant,

Karl
column3:
Unge herre,

Mine hjerteligste gratulasjoner med Deres raske forfremmelse. Deres fars anliggender gaar normalt fremover. Etter den dypt gripende begravelsen, som hele {%t:01} overvar, rykker notarer, rettsbetjenter og andre embetsmenn naa inn for aa ordne Deres fars bo. Jeg skal holde Dem underrettet om alt som skjer.

Jeg vil likevel fortelle hva jeg vet om Deres fars hemmelighet, som han naa har tatt med seg i graven. Jeg tror ikke han ville ha noe imot det, naa som De er en anerkjent fjernhandelsmann.
Dessverre kan jeg bare si at det maa ha hatt noe aa gjoere med en "Flygende handelsmann", for det mumlet Deres far alltid om i soevne. Naar jeg sent paa kvelden bar et glass vin inn til ham i arbeidsvaerelset, sov han av og til allerede paa sofaen og kastet seg urolig frem og tilbake. Ved en slik anledning fanget jeg opp dette navnet.
Marerittene hans maa stamme fra noe han opplevde paa havet i ungdommen. Deres far holdt i mange aar kontakten med en av kameratene sine fra den tiden. Kanskje kan jeg finne ut hvor han bor. Jeg skriver igjen saa snart jeg vet mer.

Deres ydmykeste tjener,

Karl

column2: Sympathy
column3: Medfoelelse

column2:
My dear Leopold!

You have probably never heard of me, but I was a good friend of your father's and have been following your career closely. Please accept my condolences on dear old Georg's sudden and unexpected death. If you are ever in trouble, you can turn to me with complete confidence.

Best wishes from the free town of {%t:04},
Patrician H. Vanderdeeken
{%-:00}HV
column3:
Min kjaere Leopold!

De har sannsynligvis aldri hoert om meg, men jeg var en god venn av Deres far og har fulgt Deres loepebane noeye. Ta imot min kondolanse ved kjaere gamle Georgs plutselige og uventede doed. Skulle De noen gang komme i knipe, kan De med full tillit henvende Dem til meg.

Beste hilsener fra den frie byen {%t:04},
Patrisier H. Vanderdeeken
{%-:00}HV

column2: The Helmsman
column3: Styrmannen

column2:
Young Sir,

I looked in your father's personal records to try and find an address for that friend that I wrote to you about. They weren't easy documents to get hold of, as the authorities are examining all of his possessions closely. But I found out something about that old colleague of his:
Jakob Blank was the helmsman of your father's Snaikka for many years and later became his associate. He then became a councillor in {%t:05}, where he presumably still lives. He used to be a regular visitor to Luebeck, but hasn't been here in the past few years. But here is the best tip that I could find. Look for a certain Jakob Blank in {%t:05}, he is also known as The Helmsman!

Your most obedient servant,

Karl
column3:
Unge herre,

Jeg har lett i Deres fars personlige papirer etter en adresse til den vennen jeg skrev om. Det var ikke lette dokumenter aa faa tak i, siden myndighetene noeye gjennomgaar alle eiendelene hans. Men jeg fant ut noe om denne gamle kameraten:
Jakob Blank var i mange aar styrmann paa Deres fars schnigge og ble siden hans kompanjong. Deretter ble han raadmann i {%t:05}, der han trolig fortsatt bor. Han pleide aa komme ofte til Luebeck, men har ikke vaert her de siste aarene. Her er i hvert fall det beste sporet jeg kunne finne. Let etter en viss Jakob Blank i {%t:05}, ogsaa kjent som Styrmannen!

Deres ydmykeste tjener,

Karl

column2: Confidential Information
column3: Fortrolige opplysninger

column2:
Honourable {%R:00} Jantzen,

You enquired about a certain Jakob Blank in {%t:05}. Let me give you some advice: forget that name and go back to {%t:01}.
I suspect, however, that you will not be prepared to take this advice, so I shall give you the official statement. The Jakob Blank matter has been declared confidential information at the command of a Hanseatic League session. Nobody will give you any information about this blackest period in the town's history.
The only way would be for another Hansa town to issue an official query to {%t:05}. But you would need to aquire the rank of councillor to put forward this query. And even then you would have to earn a certain reputation in {%t:05} before I could deal with your query. These strict guidelines are purely a precautionary measure and have been approved by the Hanseatic League session. Once you have fulfilled these conditions, I will tell you what you want to know.

Signed: The Mayor
{%+:05}
column3:
Aerede {%R:00} Jantzen,

De har spurt etter en viss Jakob Blank i {%t:05}. La meg gi Dem et raad: glem det navnet og vend tilbake til {%t:01}.
Jeg mistenker likevel at De ikke vil vaere villig til aa foelge dette raadet, saa jeg gir Dem den offisielle meddelelsen. Saken Jakob Blank er paa befaling fra en hansadag erklaert fortrolig. Ingen vil gi Dem opplysninger om denne svarteste perioden i byens historie.
Den eneste veien ville vaere at en annen hansaby retter en offisiell forespoersel til {%t:05}. Men De maatte ha raadmanns rang for aa legge frem denne forespoerselen. Og selv da maatte De oppnaa en viss anseelse i {%t:05} foer jeg kunne behandle forespoerselen Deres. Disse strenge retningslinjene er bare en forsiktighetsregel og er godkjent av hansadagen. Naar De har oppfylt disse vilkaarene, skal jeg fortelle hva De oensker aa vite.

Undertegnet: Borgermesteren
{%+:05}

column2:
Honourable {%R:00} Jantzen,

You have enquired about a certain Jakob Blank in {%t:05}. Let me give you some good advice: forget that name and go back to {%t:01}.
I suspect, however, that you will not be prepared to take this advice, so I shall give you the official statement. The Jakob Blank matter has been declared confidential information at the command of a Hanseatic League session. Nobody will give you any information about this blackest period in the town's history.
The only way would be for another Hansa town to issue an official query to {%t:05}. As you occupy the rank of {%R:00}, you need only obtain a certain reputation in Riga before I can deal with your query. These strict guidelines are purely a precautionary measure and have been approved by the Hanseatic League session.
Once you have fulfilled these conditions, I will tell you what you want to know.

Signed: The Mayor
{%+:05}
column3:
Aerede {%R:00} Jantzen,

De har spurt etter en viss Jakob Blank i {%t:05}. La meg gi Dem et godt raad: glem det navnet og vend tilbake til {%t:01}.
Jeg mistenker likevel at De ikke vil vaere villig til aa foelge dette raadet, saa jeg gir Dem den offisielle meddelelsen. Saken Jakob Blank er paa befaling fra en hansadag erklaert fortrolig. Ingen vil gi Dem opplysninger om denne svarteste perioden i byens historie.
Den eneste veien ville vaere at en annen hansaby retter en offisiell forespoersel til {%t:05}. Siden De baerer rang av {%R:00}, mangler De bare en viss anseelse i Riga foer jeg kan behandle forespoerselen Deres. Disse strenge retningslinjene er bare en forsiktighetsregel og er godkjent av hansadagen.
Naar De har oppfylt disse vilkaarene, skal jeg fortelle hva De oensker aa vite.

Undertegnet: Borgermesteren
{%+:05}

column2:
With regard to the inquiry put forward by Leopold Jantzen of {%t:0B}, concerning the matter of the exiled Jakob Blank

The following information is issued:

The person Jakob Blank was banished from {%t:05} for life over 15 years ago, for jeopardising the safety of the town and 20 further offences.
At the command of a Hanseatic League session, all Hansa towns were requested to comply with this exile.
The person's last known whereabouts is {%t:07}.
This information is confidential and for official use only.

Signed: The Mayor
{%+:05}
column3:
Angaaende forespoerselen som Leopold Jantzen fra {%t:0B} har lagt frem i saken om den forviste Jakob Blank

Foelgende opplysning gis:

Personen Jakob Blank ble for mer enn 15 aar siden forvist fra {%t:05} paa livstid for aa ha satt byens sikkerhet i fare og for 20 ytterligere forseelser.
Paa befaling fra en hansadag ble alle hansabyer anmodet om aa etterleve denne forvisningen.
Personens sist kjente oppholdssted er {%t:07}.
Denne opplysningen er fortrolig og kun til tjenestebruk.

Undertegnet: Borgermesteren
{%+:05}

column2: Good Advice
column3: Godt raad

column2:
Dear friend,

You are sticking your nose into things that you'd be better off steering clear of.
Please take this as good advice from one friend to another. 

H. Vanderdeeken
{%-:00}HV
column3:
Kjaere venn,

De stikker nesen i ting De gjorde klokest i aa holde Dem langt unna.
Ta det vennligst som et godt raad fra venn til venn.

H. Vanderdeeken
{%-:00}HV

column2: Dubious assistance
column3: Tvilsom hjelp

column2:
Honourable {%R:00} Jantzen,

I watched you questioning people in the market square and the dark alleys of {%t:07}. It attracted my attention, as such behaviour is unusual for a man of your position.
Rumour has it that you are looking for Jakob Blank. The poor fellow was well and truly taken for a ride by your 'fine' society and put himself in our protection, so that he could disappear unnoticed. I beg your pardon - I forgot to introduce myself. You don't need to know my name - all you need to know is that I run the local guild for those who aren't so well off. I am sure you see what I mean, as I don't exactly look like a pepper sack - no offence.
Anyway, we got Jakob Blank safely underground, and my colleagues did their job so well that even I couldn't tell you where he is any more. But if he had died, I would certainly have heard about it.
As you seem to be a friend of his, I am willing to assist you in your investigations. But you must prove yourself to be trustworthy in our community first, otherwise I won't be able to achieve anything for you at all. Only when your name is known in the right circles will you find that the information you want practically seeks you out.

Farewell,
\f5_X
column3:
Aerede {%R:00} Jantzen,

Jeg saa Dem spoerre ut folk paa torget og i de moerke smugene i {%t:07}. Det vakte min oppmerksomhet, siden en slik oppfoersel er uvanlig for en mann i Deres stilling.
Ryktet sier at De leter etter Jakob Blank. Den stakkars karen ble grundig lurt av Deres "fine" selskap og stilte seg under vaar beskyttelse, saa han kunne forsvinne ubemerket. Unnskyld - jeg glemte aa presentere meg. Navnet mitt trenger De ikke vite - De trenger bare aa vite at jeg leder det lokale gildet for dem som ikke har det saa godt stilt. De forstaar sikkert hva jeg mener, for jeg ser ikke akkurat ut som en rik kjoepmann - ikke vondt ment.
Uansett fikk vi Jakob Blank i sikkerhet under jorden, og kollegene mine gjorde jobben saa godt at ikke engang jeg kan si hvor han er lenger. Men hadde han doedd, ville jeg helt sikkert ha hoert om det.
Siden De synes aa vaere vennen hans, er jeg villig til aa hjelpe Dem i Deres etterforskning. Men foerst maa De vise Dem paalitelig i vaart fellesskap, ellers kan jeg ikke utrette noe som helst for Dem. Foerst naar Deres navn er kjent i de rette kretser, vil De merke at opplysningene De oensker, naermest selv oppsoeker Dem.

Farvel,
\f5_X

column2: Hideout
column3: Skjulested

column2: The person you are looking for is in {%t:09}.\n\n\\f5_X
column3: Den De leter etter, befinner seg i {%t:09}.\n\n\\f5_X

column2:
My dear Leopold Jantzen,

I tried so hard to leave my wretched past behind me. But when I heard of your father's death, I knew that you would come looking for me and that my old guilt had caught up with me again.
You have doubtless come to ask me about the "Flying Trader". I will tell you what I know, but first you must do something for me.
Take me to {%t:01}, to my old friend's grave, so that I can pray for his immortal soul and also my own!
When one of your ships is in the harbour, I shall board it.

Jakob Blank
column3:
Min kjaere Leopold Jantzen,

Jeg proevde saa hardt aa legge min elendige fortid bak meg. Men da jeg hoerte om Deres fars doed, visste jeg at De ville komme og lete etter meg, og at min gamle skyld igjen hadde innhentet meg.
De er uten tvil kommet for aa spoerre meg om "Den flygende handelsmann". Jeg skal fortelle hva jeg vet, men foerst maa De gjoere noe for meg.
Foer meg til {%t:01}, til min gamle venns grav, saa jeg kan be for hans udoedelige sjel og ogsaa for min egen!
Naar et av Deres skip ligger i havnen, gaar jeg om bord.

Jakob Blank

column2: Estate
column3: Arv

column2:
Announcement of the decision in the matter of the estate of the {%t:01} citizen and patrician, Georg Jantzen

On the basis of an old document stored in the {%t:04} and {%t:01} archives, the authorities of the aforementioned towns agree conjointly to the following order:

As specified in writing at that time, the fortune of the Jantzen family of {%t:01} passes to the patrician Vanderdeeken of {%t:04}. The aforementioned fortune comprises not only cash but also movable and immovable items such as ships and buildings.

The fortune to be transferred also includes the aforementioned assets of {%R:00} Leopold Jantzen, where such assets can be concluded to derive from his father's wealth.
This decision is intended for immediate implementation.

{%+:01}
column3:
Kunngjoering av avgjoerelsen i arvesaken etter borgeren og patrisieren fra {%t:01} Georg Jantzen

Paa grunnlag av et gammelt dokument som oppbevares i arkivene i {%t:04} og {%t:01}, blir myndighetene i nevnte byer i fellesskap enige om foelgende bestemmelse:

Som en gang skriftlig fastsatt gaar familien Jantzens formue i {%t:01} over til patrisieren Vanderdeeken fra {%t:04}. Nevnte formue omfatter ikke bare kontanter, men ogsaa loesoere og fast eiendom som skip og bygninger.

Formuen som skal overdras, omfatter dessuten nevnte eiendom tilhoerende {%R:00} Leopold Jantzen, i den grad det kan antas at den stammer fra hans fars rikdom.
Denne avgjoerelsen gjelder med umiddelbar virkning.

{%+:01}

column2:
Poor Leopold!

You must be surprised by the recent turn of events and upset about your sudden poverty. But what were you to know what good old Georg was willing to agree to, just to make it.
I said in my letter that your father and I were old friends, and although he was always condescending towards me, I now feel almost a little sympathetic about your situation - cheated by your own father, even of what you built up yourself.
Since I'm in a lenient mood, I'd like to leave you a bit of the fortune that now rightfully belongs to me. I really don't need a second trading office in {%t:01} and I have ships and cash positively coming out of my ears.
There is no need for you to thank me for my generosity - just stay out of my way in future.

H. Vanderdeeken
{%-:00}HV
column3:
Stakkars Leopold!

De maa vaere overrasket over den siste utviklingen og bedroevet over Deres plutselige fattigdom. Men hvordan skulle De kunne vite hva gamle Georg var villig til aa gjoere bare for aa lykkes?
Jeg skrev jo til Dem at Deres far og jeg var gamle venner, og selv om han alltid var nedlatende mot meg, foeler jeg naa nesten litt medlidenhet med Deres situasjon: lurt av Deres egen far, til og med for det De selv har bygget opp.
Siden jeg er i et mildt lune, vil jeg la Dem beholde litt av formuen som naa med rette tilhoerer meg. Jeg trenger virkelig ikke et nytt kontor i {%t:01}, og skip og penger har jeg mer enn nok av.
De trenger ikke takke meg for min gavmildhet; hold Dem bare unna meg i fremtiden.

H. Vanderdeeken
{%-:00}HV

column2: Journey home
column3: Hjemreise

column2:
My dear young Jantzen,

I prayed at your father's grave for both of our souls. I now feel strong enough to tell you about the "Flying Trader", although not here in {%t:01}.
The curse that afflicted your father is still working even after his death and affects the whole family - I'm lucky never to have married.
So take me back to {%t:09}, please! Once we are in my own home, I will be happy to satisfy your curiosity.
When one of your ships is in the harbour, I shall board it.

Jakob Blank
column3:
Min kjaere unge Jantzen!

Jeg har bedt ved Deres fars grav for vaare to sjeler. Naa foeler jeg meg sterk nok til aa fortelle Dem om "Den flygende kjoepmannen", men ikke her i {%t:01}.
Forbannelsen som hvilte over Deres far, virker ennaa etter hans doed og rammer hele familien; jeg var heldig som aldri giftet meg.
Foer meg derfor tilbake til {%t:09}, vaer saa snill! Vel hjemme i mitt hus skal jeg gjerne stille Deres nysgjerrighet.
Naar et av Deres skip ligger i havnen, gaar jeg om bord.

Jakob Blank

column2: Devil's Ship
column3: Djevelskip

column2:
My dear young Jantzen,

Thank you for bringing me home safely! Now, as promised, I shall tell you about the voyage when your father and I encountered the "Flying Trader".
I presume you have already heard the story of the "Flying Trader"? - Well, the "Flying Trader" is a ghost ship that drifts around the North Sea and the Baltic. Its captain was a greedy trader who even traded with the Devil to increase his fortune. And he had certainly amassed an inconceivable fortune, which he guarded jealously aboard his vast ship.
But one day, the Devil demanded his share back, and the greedy trader refused to pay.
The Devil laughed at him and said that he would get his dues somehow. He condemned the trader to stay on his gold-laden ship and never to leave it, and never to rest until the end of time. Since then, the "Flying Trader" and his ghost ship have sailed across the northern seas, bringing misfortune on any sailors that come across the ship.
That's enough for today. You can see that telling the story has made my hands tremble. Let me rest for a day, and then I will continue with the story.

Jakob Blank
column3:
Min kjaere unge Jantzen!

Takk for at De brakte meg trygt hjem! Naa skal jeg som lovet fortelle om reisen der Deres far og jeg moette "Den flygende kjoepmannen".
De har vel allerede hoert sagnet om "Den flygende kjoepmannen"? Vel, "Den flygende kjoepmannen" er et spoekelsesskip som driver omkring i Nordsjoeen og Oestersjoeen. Kapteinen var en graadig kjoepmann som til og med handlet med djevelen for aa oeke formuen sin. Og han samlet sannelig en ufattelig rikdom, som han sjalu voktet om bord paa sitt veldige skip.
Men en dag krevde djevelen sin andel, og den graadige kjoepmannen nektet aa betale.
Djevelen lo av ham og sa at han paa den ene eller andre maaten skulle faa sitt. Han doemte kjoepmannen til aa bli paa sitt gullastede skip uten noensinne aa forlate det, og aldri finne hvile til tidenes ende. Siden den gang seiler "Den flygende kjoepmannen" og hans spoekelsesskip paa de nordlige hav og bringer ulykke over hver sjoemann som krysser hans vei.
Nok for i dag. De ser at fortellingen har faatt hendene mine til aa skjelve. La meg hvile en dag, saa fortsetter jeg historien.

Jakob Blank

column2:
My dear young Jantzen,

I promised to tell you the second part of the tale today, and I am a man of my word.
In those days your father was a young trader, just as you are now. He didn't have much and was the captain of his own Snaikka, the 'Dawn Greeting', where I was his helmsman.
We were transporting goods from {%t:04} when a sail appeared on the horizon, coming towards us. We immediately realised what was approaching us, as the 'Dawn Greeting' had just run into a pocket of calm. It could only be a ghost ship flying through the waves under full sail. Everyone knew the story of the "Flying Trader" in those days, and when the ghost ship's boat rowed over to us, we both hid behind some barrels.
A ghostly figure boarded the ship and shouted for the ship's captain, but your father and I leapt into a boat and rowed away as fast as we could.
In the next harbour we came to, we asked after the 'Dawn Greeting', but nobody had seen her anywhere. There wasn't any news over the next few weeks either, so we assumed that she had sunk in the storm and cashed in the insurance policy.
But your father and I had abandoned her, although we were the most experienced sailors on board. We could never get that guilt out of our minds.
I can just see your face now - you're taking all this with a pinch of salt and will only believe what you see with your own eyes.
I could give you a map that shows where the "Flying Trader" is, but I don't want any more dead sailors on my conscience.
You must gather a robust fleet. If you have a ship that can be used as a warship (lead ship) as well, I will show you where to look. If you use a fleet like this to sail to your ruin, none of the blame can fall on me.

Jakob Blank
column3:
Min kjaere unge Jantzen!

Jeg lovet aa fortelle Dem andre del av historien i dag, og jeg er en mann som holder ord.
Dengang var Deres far en ung handelsmann, akkurat som De er naa. Han eide ikke mye og var kaptein paa sin egen snigge, "Morgenhilsenen", der jeg var hans styrmann.
Vi fraktet varer fra {%t:04} da et seil dukket opp i horisonten og styrte mot oss. Vi forstod straks hva som naermet seg, for "Morgenhilsenen" hadde nettopp kommet inn i et stilleomraade. Det kunne bare vaere et spoekelsesskip som floey over boelgene for fulle seil. Alle kjente den gang sagnet om "Den flygende kjoepmannen", og da spoekelsesskipets jolle rodde mot oss, gjemte vi oss begge bak noen toenner.
En spoekelsesaktig skikkelse kom om bord og ropte paa kapteinen, men Deres far og jeg hoppet i en jolle og rodde bort saa fort vi kunne.
I neste havn spurte vi etter "Morgenhilsenen", men ingen hadde sett den noe sted. Heller ikke de neste ukene kom det noe nytt, saa vi antok at den hadde sunket i stormen, og hevet forsikringen.
Men Deres far og jeg hadde forlatt den, enda vi var de mest erfarne sjoemennene om bord. Den skylden ble vi aldri kvitt.
Jeg ser allerede ansiktet Deres: De tar alt dette med en klype salt og tror bare paa det De ser med egne oeyne.
Jeg kunne gi Dem et kart som viser hvor "Den flygende kjoepmannen" finnes, men jeg vil ikke ha flere doede sjoemenn paa samvittigheten.
De maa samle en sterk flaate. Har De dessuten et skip som kan tjene som orlogsskip (flaggskip), skal jeg vise Dem hvor De skal lete. Seiler De med en slik flaate mot Deres undergang, kan ingen skyld falle paa meg.

Jakob Blank

column2:
What a fool I am - that's what comes of tempting fate. Everyone knows that if you escape the "Flying Trader", you mustn't tell anyone about it. And I, ever the sceptic, even offered to show you where to find it.
Ever since I blabbed to you like an idiot, the previously rich town of {%t:09} has been plagued by pestilence and failed crops. Pirates are waylaying any ships that try to provide the town with even the barest essentials.
I have wrought havoc on the only place in the world that still means anything to me. {%t:09} used to have more than 3,500 inhabitants and soon it won't even be marked on the map.
Future generations will recall: {%t:09}, that was that ruined town, destroyed by one person's foolishness. Oh, misery! I can't tell you where to find the "Flying Trader". I would just bring about even greater misfortune.
Go away, and don't come back until my homeland is safe!

Jakob Blank
column3:
For en tosk jeg er: slik gaar det naar man utfordrer skjebnen. Alle vet at den som unnslipper "Den flygende kjoepmannen", ikke maa fortelle det til noen. Og jeg, evig skeptiker, tilboed meg til og med aa vise Dem hvor den finnes.
Siden jeg snakket over meg som en idiot, er den en gang saa rike byen {%t:09} plaget av pest og uaar. Pirater overfaller hvert skip som proever aa bringe byen selv det aller mest noedvendige.
Jeg har saadd fordervelse paa det eneste stedet i verden som ennaa betyr noe for meg. {%t:09} hadde over 3 500 innbyggere og vil snart ikke engang staa paa kartet.
Kommende slekter vil huske: {%t:09}, den ruinerte byen, oedelagt av én manns daarskap. Akk og ve! Jeg kan ikke si Dem hvor "Den flygende kjoepmannen" finnes. Det ville bare bringe enda stoerre ulykke.
Gaa, og kom ikke tilbake foer mitt hjemland er reddet!

Jakob Blank

column2: Sorry figure
column3: Soergelig skikkelse

column2:
Brave Leopold!

Have you taken it upon yourself to save this godforsaken town? The citizens of {%t:09} certainly don't deserve it for harbouring that wretched sinner Blank. He was driven out of {%t:05} in disgrace, but what a joke that turned out to be. {%t:09} just flung open its gates to him because he made a generous donation to the town's coffers. That went straight into the fat councillors' pockets.
{%t:09}'s prosperous years are in the past, and believe me, even you can't bring them back!

H. Vanderdeeken
column3:
Tapre Leopold!

Har De satt Dem fore aa redde denne gudsforlatte byen? Borgerne i {%t:09} fortjener det sannelig ikke, fordi de tok imot den usle synderen Blank. Han ble jaget ut av {%t:05} i vanaere, men for en komedie det ble. {%t:09} slo portene paa vidt gap for ham, fordi han gav en gavmild gave til bykassen. Som gikk rett i lommene paa de fete raadsherrene.
{%t:09}s gode aar er forbi, og tro meg, ikke engang De kan bringe dem tilbake!

H. Vanderdeeken

column2:
Noble Jantzen!

Saviour of {%t:09}, you have shown true courage by protecting my home from the raging storms of destiny. Your success has strengthened my resolve to entrust you with my last secret: the position where the "Flying Trader" is most likely to be found. Once you have a ship that can be used as a warship, and that is therefore suitable for this delicate mission, I will give you the location at last.

Take care, and may God be with you!

Jakob Blank
column3:
Edle Jantzen!

Redningsmann for {%t:09}, De har vist ekte mot ved aa beskytte mitt hjemland mot skjebnens rasende stormer. Deres suksess har styrket min beslutning om aa betro Dem min siste hemmelighet: stedet der "Den flygende kjoepmannen" mest sannsynlig finnes. Saa snart De har et skip som kan tjene som orlogsskip og dermed egner seg for dette delikate oppdraget, skal jeg endelig gi Dem stedet.

Vaer forsiktig, og Gud vaere med Dem!

Jakob Blank

column2: Musty Old Hulk
column3: Gammel muggen holk

column2:
Honourable Sir,

We made our way to the position marked on the map and waited there. Suddenly the wind subsided and we drifted slowly with the current. There was a second ship with tattered sails floating across towards our course in a strong current. When a slight breeze started again, we boarded the ship and searched it from top to bottom.
It was nothing more than a derelict hulk, with stacks of empty, rotten chests and cases in its hold.
There was no crew on board, nor any other signs that it had been used recently. We sank the ship in the ocean according to your orders, and I am pleased to enclose a full report for you.

With nautical wishes,

Helmsman of the {%s:06}
column3:
Aerede herre!

Vi satte kurs mot stedet som var avmerket paa kartet, og ventet der. Plutselig loeyet vinden, og vi drev langsomt med stroemmen. Et annet skip med fillete seil drev inn mot kursen vaar i en sterk stroem. Da en lett bris igjen blaaste opp, entret vi skipet og gjennomsoekte det fra topp til bunn.
Det var ikke annet enn en forlatt holk, med hauger av tomme, raatne kister og kasser i lasterommet.
Det var ingen mannskap om bord, og heller ikke noe annet tegn paa at den var brukt nylig. Vi senket skipet i havet etter Deres ordre, og jeg har gleden av aa vedlegge en fullstendig rapport.

Med sjoemannshilsen,

Styrmannen paa {%s:06}

column2:
Brave Jantzen!

I have heard about your encounter with the ghost ship. As you and your entire crew have escaped with your lives, it would seem that the curse of the "Flying Trader" has finally been broken. Seafaring is therefore greatly indebted to you, but I am even more indebted to you, for you have lifted a dark shadow from my soul. There is a rumour that you are now hoping to be elected mayor in Bremen, so that you can put that self-satisfied Vanderdeeken in his place. I would love to be there with you, but, now that I am free of my terrible burden, I imagine I shall soon be peacefully entering the realms of the dead.

Farewell,

Jakob Blank
column3:
Tapre Jantzen!

Jeg har hoert om Deres moete med spoekelsesskipet. Siden De og hele mannskapet Deres kom fra det med livet i behold, ser forbannelsen over "Den flygende kjoepmannen" endelig ut til aa vaere brutt. Sjoefarten staar altsaa i stor gjeld til Dem, men jeg enda mer, for De har fjernet en moerk skygge fra min sjel. Det sies at De naa haaper aa bli valgt til borgermester i Bremen, for aa sette den hovne Vanderdeeken paa plass. Hvor gjerne ville jeg ikke vaert der med Dem, men naa som jeg er fri for min fryktelige byrde, gaar jeg vel snart i fred inn i de doedes rike.

Farvel,

Jakob Blank

column2: Mayor
column3: Borgermester

column2:
Young Sir,

I would like to congratulate you on your recent deeds. There has been a splendid atmosphere in the house since the latest news about you arrived.
News of your plan to become mayor of {%t:04} has already spread throughout the Hanseatic League. Even a cousin from Novgorod contacted us to wish you luck.
The inhabitants of your old home town will certainly be sorry to lose their most celebrated {%R:00}, but everybody is hoping that you will teach the unpopular Vanderdeeken a lesson by becoming mayor of his home town.

Your most obedient servant,

Karl
column3:
Unge herre!

Jeg vil gratulere Dem med Deres siste bedrifter. Siden de siste nyhetene om Dem kom, hersker det en straalende stemning i huset.
Nyheten om Deres plan om aa bli borgermester i {%t:04} har allerede spredt seg over hele Hansaen. Til og med en fetter fra Novgorod har tatt kontakt for aa oenske Dem lykke til.
Innbyggerne i Deres gamle hjemby vil nok savne sin mest beroemte {%R:00}, men alle haaper at De vil gi den upopulaere Vanderdeeken en lekse ved aa bli borgermester i hans egen by.

Deres tro tjener,

Karl

column2: Legacy
column3: Testamente

column2:
Now then, young Jantzen!

So you think you can offer me your services in Bremen? Or maybe not - I hear that you want to become mayor of my town. And the rabble and fat cats are encouraging you in this recklessness.
Let me give you this warning: the people that are so fond of you at the moment are driven by envy. They envy my wealth and power, but they secretly admire and fear me.
They would never utter a single word against me and I'll give you some honest advice - do the same thing.
Well, you may be able to sink rotten ships, but in my view you're nothing more than a ne'er-do-well, brought up by his father to have too high an opinion of himself.

H. Vanderdeeken
{%-:00}HV
column3:
Naa, unge Jantzen!

Saa De tror De kan tilby meg Deres tjenester i Bremen? Eller kanskje ikke: jeg hoerer at De vil bli borgermester i min by. Og poebelen og storkarene oppmuntrer Dem i dette overmotet.
La meg advare Dem: de som naa setter saa stor pris paa Dem, drives av misunnelse. De misunner meg min rikdom og min makt, men i hemmelighet beundrer og frykter de meg.
De ville aldri si et vondt ord om meg, og jeg gir Dem et oppriktig raad: gjoer det samme.
De kan kanskje senke raatne skip, men for meg er De ikke annet enn en doegenikt som Deres far oppdro med altfor hoeye tanker om seg selv.

H. Vanderdeeken
{%-:00}HV

column2: Honesty
column3: Aerlighet

column2:
My dear colleague, Mr Jantzen,

I am truly concerned about your soul. Your father had to pledge the full extent of his future wealth to make half as much progress, and I can't imagine what shady deals you have done to propell you upwards so quickly.
I can't believe that the sudden wealth that you are flaunting with such a lack of restraint is the result of good, honest hard work. I do hope you aren't making the same mistake your father did!

H. Vanderdeeken
{%-:00}HV
column3:
Min kjaere kollega, herr Jantzen!

Jeg er virkelig bekymret for Deres sjel. Deres far maatte pantsette hele sin fremtidige formue for aa komme halvveis, og jeg toer ikke tenke paa hvilke lyssky forretninger som har drevet Dem saa raskt oppover.
Jeg kan ikke tro at den plutselige rikdommen De saa ugjenert viser frem, er frukten av godt, aerlig og hardt arbeid. Jeg haaper De ikke gjoer den samme feilen som Deres far!

H. Vanderdeeken
{%-:00}HV

column2:
Dear Mayor Jantzen,

Some time ago, a letter postmarked {%t:09} arrived, addressed to "Mayor Jantzen of {%t:04}". We assumed that this was a mistake and returned it to the sender. But the letter came back to us, again postmarked {%t:09}, and lay forgotten until your inauguration reminded me of it again.
It seems to me that the letter must be intended for you and, now that you are mayor, I can give it to you.

{%t:04} Post office
column3:
Kjaere borgermester Jantzen!

For en tid siden kom et brev stemplet i {%t:09}, adressert til "borgermester Jantzen i {%t:04}". Vi trodde det var en feil og sendte det tilbake til avsenderen. Men brevet kom tilbake til oss, igjen stemplet i {%t:09}, og ble liggende glemt til Deres tiltredelse minnet meg om det.
Det forekommer meg at brevet maa vaere ment for Dem, og naa som De er borgermester, kan jeg overrekke det.

Postkontoret i {%t:04}

column2: Guilt
column3: Skyld

column2:
\f1_Here is the letter that was kept for you.
\f3_

\r{%t:09}, {%D:10}
\lWhat a wretched sinner I am!

A short time ago, one of my few old friends visited me in the bed where I shall soon be meeting my maker. He was to tell me every detail that he knew of the events surrounding your voyage to the ghost ship. It was with horror that I learnt from his account that you did not actually make the voyage yourself.
Of course, this changes everything. As you had your father's money in your pocket, you should have seen the ghost ship. Once again, I have brought twice, three times as much guilt upon myself and am writing this letter so that I can warn you at least of the impending doom.

Didn't you mention last time we met that you were now mayor of {%t:04}? If that is the case, this letter will doubtless have reached you promptly, and at least you will be able to save your soul. But one thing at a time:
I didn't tell you the whole truth about the "Flying Trader" and my encounter with the ghost ship.

Anyone who encounters the ghost ship with a pure conscience and without desire for profit will see nothing more than a ship that has been weathered over the centuries, and is in absolutely no danger.
But anyone on board with greed in his heart or who carries any of the ghost ship's treasure in his purse will be greeted by the apparition of the miserly trader, who will propose a deal. Those who accept will receive a share of the trader's treasure and will sell the souls of any respectable sailors aboard the ship in return.
The treasure is bewitched and multiplies as if by itself, but it is cursed to find its way back to its master and ultimately to bring the unlawful owner nothing but misfortune.

In those days, your father's business was not going very well and he had fallen for a beautiful lady in Luebeck, whose father wanted nothing to do with a poor son-in-law. I had gambled away a lot of money, and so before that fateful voyage, we found ourselves sitting in an inn in Bremen discussing our problems, when a stranger approached our table. He knew all about our difficulties and offered to help us. All he wanted in return was a fair share of our future wealth. We agreed, having nothing to lose, and he told us that on our next voyage we would happen upon a ship with which we could conduct the transaction of our lives.
I don't need to tell you the details of what happened next, as you have surely guessed them already. We sold the 'Dawn Greeting' to the "Flying Trader" and made it to dry land with a rowing boat full of gold.
From then on, fortune seemed to smile upon us. Your father got his girl and forged a fabulous career for himself in {%t:01}. I paid my debts and won plenty more money besides, until one day the stranger appeared again. First of all, he demanded that your father give him his sweet little daughter. Then he came to me: I refused to give in to his demands and was chased from what was then my home, labelled a common criminal. Since then, I went on the run time and time again and lost touch with your father. It was only in {%t:09} that I found my way back to a reasonably normal life, although I never touched the money that I had left. And now I shall have to go to my grave with new sins because I failed to tell you the whole truth in time. All I can do now is advise you to hide all of your father's money and all that I am leaving you for safe keeping. Do not touch it, and under no circumstances must you use it in an attempt to increase it, otherwise the curse of the "Flying Trader" will find you and you will know no more peace in this world!

Farewell,

Jakob Blank
column3:
\f1_Her er brevet som har blitt oppbevart for Dem.
\f3_

\r{%t:09}, {%D:10}
\lFor en elendig synder jeg er!

For en tid siden besoekte en av mine faa gamle venner meg ved leiet der jeg snart skal moete min Skaper. Han skulle fortelle meg hver detalj han kjente til om Deres reise til spoekelsesskipet. Med gru fikk jeg vite av hans beretning at De ikke selv foretok reisen.
Det endrer selvsagt alt. Siden De bar Deres fars penger i lommen, burde De ha sett spoekelsesskipet. Nok en gang har jeg paadratt meg dobbel, tredobbel skyld, og jeg skriver dette brevet for i det minste aa advare Dem mot den truende fordervelsen.

Nevnte De ikke ved vaart siste moete at De naa er borgermester i {%t:04}? Er det slik, har dette brevet sikkert naadd Dem raskt, og De kan i det minste redde Deres sjel. Men la meg begynne fra begynnelsen:
Jeg fortalte ikke hele sannheten om "Den flygende kjoepmannen" og mitt moete med spoekelsesskipet.

Den som moeter spoekelsesskipet med ren samvittighet og uten vinningslyst, ser ikke annet enn et skip merket av aarhundrer og er ikke i noen fare.
Men den som er om bord med graadighet i hjertet, eller baerer noe av spoekelsesskipets skatt i pungen, blir moett av gjenferdet til den gjerrige kjoepmannen, som foreslaar en handel. De som tar imot den, faar en del av kjoepmannens skatt og selger til gjengjeld sjelene til alle hederlige sjoemenn om bord.
Skatten er forhekset og formerer seg liksom av seg selv, men den er forbannet: den finner tilbake til sin herre og bringer til slutt den urettmessige eieren ikke annet enn ulykke.

Dengang gikk Deres fars forretninger ikke saerlig godt, og han hadde forelsket seg i en vakker dame fra Luebeck, hvis far ikke ville vite av en fattig svigersoenn. Jeg hadde tapt mye penger paa spill, og saa satt vi foer den skjebnesvangre reisen paa et vertshus i Bremen og snakket om vaare sorger, da en fremmed kom bort til bordet vaart. Han visste alt om vaare vansker og tilboed seg aa hjelpe oss. Alt han ville ha til gjengjeld, var en rimelig andel av vaar fremtidige rikdom. Vi sa ja, for vi hadde ingenting aa tape, og han sa at vi paa vaar neste reise ville stoete paa et skip som vi ville gjoere vaart livs handel med.
Jeg trenger ikke fortelle hva som skjedde siden, det har De sikkert allerede gjettet. Vi solgte "Morgenhilsenen" til "Den flygende kjoepmannen" og naadde fast land i en robaat full av gull.
Siden den gang syntes lykken aa smile til oss. Deres far fikk sin pike og gjorde en eventyrlig karriere i {%t:01}. Jeg betalte gjelden min og vant dessuten mye penger, inntil den fremmede en dag dukket opp igjen. Foerst krevde han at Deres far skulle gi ham sin soete lille datter. Saa kom han til meg: jeg nektet aa boeye meg for kravene hans og ble jaget ut av det som den gang var mitt hjem, stemplet som en simpel forbryter. Siden har jeg flyktet igjen og igjen og mistet kontakten med Deres far. Foerst i {%t:09} vendte jeg tilbake til et noenlunde normalt liv, selv om jeg aldri roerte pengene jeg hadde igjen. Og naa maa jeg gaa i graven med nye synder, fordi jeg ikke fortalte Dem hele sannheten i tide. Alt jeg kan gjoere naa, er aa raade Dem til aa gjemme alle Deres fars penger og alt jeg etterlater Dem, i forvaring. Roer det ikke, og bruk det under ingen omstendigheter til aa proeve aa formere det, ellers vil forbannelsen over "Den flygende kjoepmannen" finne Dem, og De vil ikke kjenne ro mer i denne verden!

Farvel,

Jakob Blank

column2:
Accursed Jantzen!

Why do you always have to meddle in things you don't understand?
You evidently have a certain talent for manipulating people, Mr Mayor of {%t:04}.
That's how you've managed to become my superior here in my home town of {%t:04}, not that that matters, as I still have countless other titles!
You can gloat and rejoice as much as you like, but I'll get what's mine in the end. Sooner or later we will meet again - and that's a promise.

H. Vanderdeeken
{%-:00}HV
column3:
Forbannede Jantzen!

Hvorfor maa De alltid blande Dem inn i ting De ikke forstaar?
De har aapenbart et visst talent for aa manipulere folk, herr borgermester i {%t:04}.
Slik har De blitt min overordnede her i min hjemby {%t:04}, ikke at det betyr noe, for jeg har ennaa utallige andre titler!
De kan fryde Dem og glede Dem saa mye De vil, men til slutt faar jeg det som er mitt. Foer eller siden moetes vi igjen, det lover jeg.

H. Vanderdeeken
{%-:00}HV

column2:
{%7:03}{%N:0A},

The legend of the Kobold is circulating amongst the crew again. I have heard of instances where the crew have got so worked up that they have put the whole ship in danger.
I shall be harder on the sailors than usual, so that they can get this dangerous superstition out of their heads as quickly as possible.

Helmsman of the {%s:04}
column3:
{%7:03}{%N:0A},

Sagnet om skipsnissen gaar igjen rundt blant mannskapet. Jeg har hoert om tilfeller der mannskaper ble saa oppjaget at de satte hele skipet i fare.
Jeg skal vaere strengere mot sjoemennene enn vanlig, saa de fortest mulig faar denne farlige overtroen ut av hodet.

Styrmannen paa {%s:04}

column2: Anxiety
column3: Uro

column2:
{%7:03}{%N:0A},

Once again, those gullible scaredicats have picked up something about the Kobold. It is this very spirit that protects every ship, and legend says that if he should ever disembark, the ship would be lost, including its crew and cargo. You will have heard the tale that the Kobold is supposed to show himself just before he leaves the ship. But now these tars reckon they're seeing the Kobold leering out at them from behind every plank.
Morale is not at its highest, so it might be better if you took care of this yourself!

Helmsman of the {%s:04}
column3:
{%7:03}{%N:0A},

Nok en gang har disse godtroende reddharene snappet opp noe om skipsnissen. Det er nettopp denne aanden som beskytter hvert skip, og sagnet sier at om han noen gang gaar i land, er skipet tapt, med mannskap og last. De har vel hoert at skipsnissen skal vise seg like foer han forlater skipet. Men naa mener disse sjoeulkene aa se nissen glise mot dem bak hver planke.
Moralen er ikke paa topp, saa det var kanskje bedre om De tok Dem av det selv!

Styrmannen paa {%s:04}

column2:
{%7:03}{%N:0A},

One of the older sailors told the younger ones that the Kobold leaves any ship whose owner acts in a way that is displeasing to God.
I have managed to calm the crew down by telling them that you were renowned for your honesty throughout the entire Hanseatic League. Now everybody on board is concentrating on their duties again.

Helmsman of the {%s:04}
column3:
{%7:03}{%N:0A},

En av de eldre sjoemennene fortalte de yngre at skipsnissen forlater ethvert skip der eieren handler paa en maate som mishager Gud.
Jeg har faatt roet mannskapet ved aa si at De er kjent i hele Hansaen for Deres aerlighet. Naa konsentrerer alle om bord seg igjen om pliktene sine.

Styrmannen paa {%s:04}

column2:
{%7:03}{%N:0A},

This time, even members of our own crew say they have seen the ghost ship. And now that the crew has heard talk in the {%t:07} taverns about a ship that is long overdue, there are rumours going round that it has been captured by the 'Flying Trader'.
You will not be surprised to learn that all this unfortunate speculation has damaged the crew's morale.

Helmsman of the {%s:04}
column3:
{%7:03}{%N:0A},

Denne gangen sier til og med folk fra vaart eget mannskap at de har sett spoekelsesskipet. Og naa som mannskapet har hoert snakk i kneipene i {%t:07} om et skip som lenge har vaert forsinket, gaar det rykter om at det er kapret av "Den flygende kjoepmannen".
Det vil ikke overraske Dem at all denne uheldige spekulasjonen har skadet mannskapets moral.

Styrmannen paa {%s:04}
